# Isaiah 50-66

## ANNOTATIONS ON THE BOOK OF THE PROPHET ISAIAH

### CHAPTER 50

**V. 1.** *{Thus saith the Lord*} This chapter, and the next, are not improbably deemed to make one sermon, spent in a conviction of the Jewish people, as authors of their own forlorn condition; together with a justification of God and his ministers, against them, verse 1–9, an exhortation to the godly party, among them, to rest and rely upon God, in these calamitous times; with a sad commination to those that trusted to aught else, verse 10,11, a consolation and encouragement, by promised protection, against their enemies' power, unto those, that so did, chapter 51:1–8, a pathetical supplication of them, unto God, to manifest his power, formerly showed in their delivery, together with a gracious answer of God thereunto, verse 9–16, and a compellation of God's people thereupon, calling upon them, to raise up themselves, and come out of that desolate condition, in which they had a long time lain, verse 17–23.

*{where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away?*} The people of the Jews, during the time of their captivity, seemed to be in a manner divorced from God, and by God, whom they had been formerly joined to in marriage, Jeremiah 3:8,14. See chapter 49:21. Now whereas, among that people, many times, for very frivolous occasions, men were wont to put away their wives, Matthew 19:3, but the law then commanded that a writing, or bill of divorce should be given them, Deuteronomy 24:1, wherein also some suppose (but that without ground) that for saving the woman's reputation in such case, there should, if not, the particular ground of the divorce be declared, yet a clearing of her from any imputation of disloyalty. But howsoever it be for the latter, in allusion to the thing itself, God here calls upon his people to produce the bill of divorce, by which he had discharged them, and himself of them, as implying, that either none such could be produced, for that he had not, in any such manner, put them away; but they had willfully, of their own accord, gone away from him, chapter 1:4. Or, if any such were extant, and could be produced, it would thereby appear, that the breach began on their part; that they had rather forsaken him, than he them, and that it was not for any slight occasion, but for their disloyalty, that they had been cast off; Jeremiah 3:1,2,20, Hosea 2:2,5. For whereas some interpreters would so mince the matter, as if the Jewish people, though they had been, by God, severed, as from bed and board only for a time; during their deportation, and the destruction of the temple; yet they had not been divorced from him, nor had joined themselves in marriage to any other, though they were defiled with many, which therefore nothing hindered, but that they might be received again by God, upon their return: Yet the contrary hereunto appears, both that God had put them away, as by a bill of divorce; and that their carriage had been such, as came within compass of that law; and that God, notwithstanding as not obliged thereby, nor taking advantage of it, would again receive such, as he had so repudiated upon their return, Jeremiah 3:1,2,6,7,8,12,14. Nor will that hold, which the Jewish doctors have here, that Jeremy speaks of Israel, the ten tribes, that were never to return, or have king again, and are therefore, said to have had a bill of divorce given them; whereas Esay speaks of Judah, that were to return from captivity, and to have Messiah for their king: For return is both proffered, and promised, as well to the one, as the other; and Christ as a common king to them both, Jeremiah 3:12–14 & 31:1,4–6, Ezekiel 37:16–25, Hosea 3:4,5. Yet true it is, that God did never utterly cast off the whole body of his people, but had his reserved ones, in all times, among them, Romans 11:1–5.

*{where is*} Hebrew, *where that:* but the pronoun demonstrative, is put for the verb substantive, as chapter 49:21 & 66:1.

*{your mother's*} The Jewish church and state, is resembled by a woman, a mother; whose sons, her people, are said to be, chapter 49:20,21. So Hosea 2:2.

*{bill of divorcement*} Hebrew, *book of abscission,* or *cutting off,* Deuteronomy 24:1, so called, because the woman was thereby declared to be cut off from her husband, unto whom she had formerly been joined in wedlock.

*{I have put away*} Hebrew, *sent away,* or *dismissed,* Deuteronomy 24:1,3,4. So of Israel, or the ten tribes, Jeremiah 3:8,9, Hosea 2, verse 2.

*{or which of my creditors is it, to which I have sold you?*} Among the Jews, parents many times falling behindhand, or being in want, did sell their children to help themselves, or pay their debts, Exodus 21:7, and their creditors, unto whom, they were not able to make satisfaction otherwise, took their children for their debt, 2 Kings 4:1, Matthew 18:25. God alluding therefore thereunto, wills them to name the creditor, to whom upon such occasion, he had sold them; which was a thing that could not be, God being not a debtor, or owing aught unto any, Romans 11:35,36.

*{my creditors*} Hebrew, *lenders,* Deuteronomy 24:11, chapter 24:1.

*{behold, for your iniquities have you sold yourselves*} They rather had sold themselves unto sin, to purchase liberty for their inordinate desires and delights, 1 Kings 21:25, chapter 52:3, John 8:34, Romans 6:15,16, 2 Peter 2:19. Or, *ye are sold:* For in the Hebrew it is no more, and although the passive form is in Hebrew used sometime in a reciprocal notion, as chapter 1:15,24 & 45:20, yet there is no necessity of it here: for it is well known, that for some offenses, men were sometime, by law, sold, Exodus 22:3. But the ground, and cause of the sale, was then from themselves. And so was it with this people, when God sold them, sometime, unto slavery, for their sins, Judges 2:13,14 & 3:7,8, Psalm 44:11,12.

*{and for your transgressions is your mother put away*} Or, *dismissed,* as verse 1. *for your transgressions is your mother dismissed;*] as if the children were so exceedingly unruly, and rebellious, and the mother so fondly addicted to them, that without casting out both, no quietness could be had, Genesis 21:10, Galatians 4:30. Or, indeed, because the state or church, resembled by the person of a mother, and the persons, or people, in the generality, at least, of whom the church and state did consist, as of limbs a body, 1 Corinthians 12:12, but resembled by sons, or children, are, in effect, one and the same. See on chapter 62:5. Howsoever we take it, the meaning is, that God had not out of any peevish, or selfish humor, cast off their mother, and them, with her; but for her, and their disloyal and rebellious carriages, which yet, if they put away repented of, and reformed, they might be received, and taken in again, Jeremiah 3:1,12,14, Hosea 2:4,5.

**V. 2.** *{wherefore when I came, was there no man? when I called was there none to answer?*} Hebrew, *why came I, and there was not a man?* Or, *not any one?* (as Jeremiah 5:1, implying a general defection, chapter 59:16 & 64:6,7.) *I called, and there was no answerer,* or, *none that would answer:* a note of willful obstinacy, Proverbs 29:19. For the syntax, see the like, Genesis 14:14, chapter 30:20 & 44:14. As their refractory, and rebellious courses, not any unkindness, or harsh carriage, on God's part, had procured their captivity, and brought them into that desolate and disconsolate condition; so it was not any unwillingness thereunto, or inability on God's part, who had never willingly cast them off, that retarded their delivery. It was their obstinate refusal to return to God by repentance, though by his prophets, oft and earnestly inviting, and inciting them thereunto, that kept them still in this deplorable plight, chapter 5.43.1. & 65:2, Jeremiah 5:3,23,25 & 8:6 & 11:7,8, Zechariah 7:11,12.

*{I came*} He came to them, by his ministers, and messengers, 2 Chronicles 36:15, Jeremiah 15:19 & 35:14, as to those other, Ephesians 2:17, 1 Peter 3:20, yea, not by his servants only, but by his Son, Matthew 21:34,37, John 1:11, unto which coming (but groundlessly) some restrain this.

*{Is my hand shortened, at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver?*} Am I not as well able to rescue and deliver you out of the hands of those, that hold you in thraldom now, as in time past? out of Babylon, as out of Egypt? See chapter 59:1,2.

*{shortened at all*} Or, *any whit shortened,* Hebrew, *shortening shortened.* See Numbers 11:21.

*{that it cannot redeem*} Or, *rescue:* as Psalm 107:2. Hebrew, *from rescue,* or *redemption:* as, *from saving, from hearing,* chapter 59:1.

*{Behold, at my rebuke, I dry up the sea*} Or, *with my rebuke, I can dry up the sea:* for these futures, have oft a potential notion in them. See on chapter 49:15. I am able to do it with a word of my mouth; and to rescue your forefathers from eminent, and imminent destruction: I sometime did it, Exodus 14:21,29, chapter 15:10. *He rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up,* Psalm 106:9, for though God's rebuke be not a verbal, but a real rebuke, yet what therein he does, he does it with as much ease, as if he did it with a word, Psalm 76:6.

*{I make the rivers a wilderness*} Or, *I can make* (as before; to wit, *with my rebuke,* to be supplied from the former branch, as chapter 47:9.) *the floods* (as Psalm 93:3, the floods, both of the Red Sea, and of Jordan, Joshua 2:10 & 3:14, though the former principally here intended,) *as a wilderness:* (as dry as wastes are wont to be) or, *as a plain,* as easy to pass, as any plain ground. See Lamentations 5:9. So Psalm 107:33, *He turneth floods into a wilderness;* and, chapter 42:15, *I will make floods, lands,* or, *dry lands:* and chapter 63:13, *He led them through the deep, as an horse in the wilderness,* or, *on the plain.* See chapter 51:10.

*{their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst*} The like is intimated, chapter 19:5–8,10, Ezekiel 29:4,5, Hosea 4:3, Zephaniah 1:3.

*{their fish stinketh*} So when the waters were turned into blood, Exodus 7:18.

*{because there is no water*} For want of water. Hebrew, *from no water being,* as chapter 5:9, *from no inhabitant being.*

*{dieth for thirst*} Hebrew, *with thirst:* as Hosea 2:5. See Psalm 105:29.

**V. 3.** *{I clothe the heavens with blackness, and make sackcloth their covering*} Or, *I can clothe* (as before, verse 2.) *the heavens with blackness.* I can cause the heavenly bodies to withdraw all their light, as if they were turned into darkness, in token of my displeasure, chapter 13:10, Ezekiel 32:7, Joel 2:31, Amos 5:8, Matthew 24:29 and 27:45, as I did also sometime in Egypt, Exodus 10:21–23.

*{make sackcloth their covering*} Make them as black, as if they were covered over with sackcloth; such stuff, as the Kedaren curtains were made of, Canticles 1:5, and as they used to cover themselves with, in time of solemn humiliation and mourning, Psalm 35:9,10, Jonas 3:6,8. So Revelation 6:12, *The sun became black, as sackcloth of hair,* as sackcloth made of goats' black hair. Hebrew, *sack;* as chapter 3:24.

**V. 4.** *{The Lord God hath given me the tongue of the learned*} In the passage ensuing, the prophet maintains his own ministry, by relating of God's furnishing him with endowments fit for it, and his faithful discharge of his duty therein: and that partly, to justify God himself; of whom before, verse 2, who had come to them, and called upon them, to reclaim, and reduce them, by no sorry silly person; but such as whom having assigned unto that office, he had sufficiently qualified for the same: and who had accordingly applied themselves diligently and constantly thereunto, notwithstanding all the obstructions and oppositions they had met with, in the execution thereof: and there was nothing, therefore, wanting on his part, for the bringing of them home again to him, chapter 5:4, and withal, to clear himself, concerning his own carriage in his place, against all his opposites, corrupt princes, false prophets, and refractory people, that had bandied together, and bent themselves jointly against him, using him with all scorn and contempt: and so it has reference to his former discourse; and partly, also, to strengthen thereby, the pious party among them, in firmer assurance of those gracious promises of God, wherewith he was sent unto them, that his messages, concerning them, might be the more efficacious with them, for their consolation and encouragement: and so it looks forward to what ensues, verse 10, chapter 51:1,4,7. See the like passages in the apostle Paul, concerning his apostleship, Romans 11:13, 1 Corinthians 4:1–19 and 9:1,2 and 15:10, 2 Corinthians 1:12 and 2:14–17 and 3 and 4:1,2 and 5:20 and 6:1–10 and 10 and 11 and 12 and 13:1–10. It is true, that divers interpreters understand all this, as spoken in the person of Christ; and there are divers passages that very fitly agree in to him, and whereof concerning Esay, there is no mention, in the holy story: but as some other, of prime note, well observe, the same may be said of sundry particulars, in Psalm 22 and 40 and 69, applied expressly unto our Savior Christ, in the New Testament, Matthew 27:34,35,43,46 and Hebrews 10:5–10, and yet, none make doubt, but that those psalms but as they were by David composed; so in his own person, they concerned him: and that, in all likelihood, in some particulars, which yet are not found expressly recorded in the story of him.

*{The Lord God*} Hebrew, *Adonai Jehovah;* the *Sovereign self-being:* and so verse 5.

*{hath given me*} He, from whom every good gift, and endowment, comes, John 3:27, Romans 12:3,6, 1 Corinthians 4:7 and 7:25 and 12:4–6, James 1:17.

*{me*} The prophet Esay. See chapter 8:11 and 49:1,2, and Jesus Christ much more, John 3:34, Colossians 2:3,9, whom he sent furnished, beyond measure with all abilities, requisite, for information, and consolation, of his elect.

*{the tongue of the learned*} The word signifies one well skilled in spiritual doctrine, in divine truths. Such an one, as our Savior speaks of, Matthew 13:52, for the word there used, fitly answers this. See on chapter 8:16.

*{that I might know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary*} Hebrew, *to season a word,* or *timely,* or, *seasonably, to deal a word,* (for the word, nowhere else found, comes from that which signifies *time,* or, *season,* Ecclesiastes 3:1,7, and imports the *timely,* or, *seasonable,* doing of aught;) *to the weary,* that is, to minister a word of comfort and consolation to a soul, that lies under heavy pressures, and is almost tired out with them, chapter 61:1,2, Matthew 11:28, as another *Barnabas,* a *son of consolation,* Acts 4:36, and do it in due season, when it is most needful, and may be most advantageous to the poor distressed soul. See Proverbs 25:11, Ecclesiastes 3:11. Some render it, *to him that is thirsty,* expounding it, to such as thirst after knowledge, are desirous to hear, and learn: but the word signifies, not *thirsty,* but *faint,* and *weary,* Psalm 107:5, chapter 40:28,29.

*{he awakeneth morning by morning*} Or, *he awakeneth me morning by morning:* the pronoun wanting, as chapter 46:3. Or it may be carried on to the next clause, *he wakeneth,* or, *stirreth up,* (as Haggai 1:14, Zechariah 4:1.) *morning by morning,* or, *morning after morning,* (Hebrew, *in the morning, in the morning,* that is every morning: as chapter 28:19.) *he stirreth up,* or, *raiseth up,* (I say) *mine ear* (every morning) *to hear as the learned.* He does incessantly, day after day; and very early, every day, not by fits and starts only stir up my spirit, and instruct me, Psalm 16:7, John 5:20 & 8:28.

*{he wakeneth mine ear*} He stirs up my spirit; as Ezra 1:1.

*{to hear*} To listen, and attend diligently, to what he is pleased to disclose unto me, Psalm 85:8, Habakkuk 2:1, Acts 16:14, Revelation 2:7,11.

*{as the learned*} As teachers are wont to excite, and stir up their scholars; and doctors, their disciples: and so the word of *stirring up* is to be supplied from the former branch; or, as those that are not *learners* only; but *learned:* and that affect, and desire to be further taught, and more learned are wont to hearken and attend, and then is the word of *hearing,* to be thence supplied, *as the learned* use *to hear.* The word first, and properly, signifies one *taught;* in the next place, one *learned.* See chapter 8:16 & 54:13.

**V. 5.** *{The Lord God*} As before, verse 4.

*{hath opened mine ear*} Or, *opened mine ear;* to wit, then, when, he called me to this office, as he *touched my tongue* then, to refine it, and thereby to enable me, to speak in fit, and due manner to his people, chapter 6:7, Jeremiah 1:9 & 15:19, so he *opened mine ear* also, to hearken to him, to receive the word from him, as chapter 35:5, and to be dutiful and obedient to him, in whatsoever he should require of me, or set me about, as Jeremiah 1:7. For *hearing,* in these, and the like phrases, implies as well obedience, as attention, 1 Samuel 15:22,23, Psalm 81:8,11,13. See somewhat the like, of David, and of Christ, Psalm 40:6, though the word there used, be diverse from this, and, by some deemed to look another way. But of Christ's obedience to God his Father, see Luke 2:49, John 4:34 & 5:19,36 and 6:48 & 8:26–29 & 17:49,50, Philippians 2:7,8, Hebrews 5:8, of persons disposed the contrary way, Psalm 58:4,5, chapter 28:11,12 & 30:9 and 33:15 & 42:18–20, Jeremiah 6:10, Zechariah 7:11, Acts 7:51,57.

*{and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back*} Or, *I was not disobedient,* (as Psalm 105:28.) *nor turned backward,* Psalm 44:18. I did neither hang back, (as Moses sometime, Exodus 3:11,13 and 4:1,10,13.) nor refuse to go, when God sent me; as Jonas, Jonah 1:3, but offered myself freely, and readily, to his call: nor did I afterward flinch, or shrink back, for any opposition, or evil usage, I met with: as Jeremy sometime, Jeremiah 20:7,9. See chapter 6:8. See also of David, and of Christ, Psalm 40:7,8, John 14:31, Philippians 2:8, Hebrews 10:5, of Paul, Acts 26:19, Galatians 1:15,16.

**V. 6.** *{I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them, that plucked off my hair*} How these particular evil usages were by Esay endured, no story informs us: yet that he did undergo much opprobrious usage, and many affronts, in the prosecution of his prophetical employment, from the profane great ones of the times, under Ahaz especially, there need no great doubt be made. See chapter 28:14. But of our Savior, we have express and pregnant relations of what in this kind he endured, Matthew 26:27 & 27:26, Luke 22:63,64, John 18:23. See on verse 4.

*{my cheeks*} Job 16:10, Lamentations 3:30, Micah 5:1.

*{plucked off the hair*} To wit, of the beard, Ezra 9:2, which does clothe the cheeks also, as well as the chin; for though the word *hair,* be not expressed in the original, which has reference only to the *pluckers off,* yet the word does properly and peculiarly, signify a *plucking off of hair;* and is well, therefore so rendered, both here, and Nehemiah 13:25.

*{I hid my not face from shame, and spitting*} Shame, for, shameful and opprobrious usage, Micah 2:6.

*{spitting*} Hebrew, *spittle,* Job 7:19. See Numbers 12:14, Luke 18:32, Job 30:10, a practice used, as well in way of detestation, as of contempt, Matthew 26:47 & 27:30, Mark 14:65.

**V. 7.** *{For the Lord God will help me*} Or, *but,* or, *Yet, the Lord,* or, *Sovereign, Jehovah;* as before, verse 4,5, and again, verse 9. Hebrew, *And:* as chapter 42:25. His encouragement to persevere, from assurance of God, assistance. So verse 9. See the like, Psalm 118:7, Jeremiah 15:26, chapter 42:10,13,14.

*{therefore shall I not be confounded*} Or, *ashamed;* as chapter 54:4, Jeremiah 3:3 & 8:12, for it is the same word, in notion, and notation, with that which was rendered *shame* before, verse 7, and has reference thereunto; as if he had said, their shameful usage of me, shall never shame me, shall never make me ashamed. See Acts 5:41.

*{therefore have I set my face, as a flint*} A form of speech, noting extreme obstinacy in some, Jeremiah 5:3, Zechariah 7:12, settled and fixed constancy in others, Ezekiel 3:8,9, and so here.

*{and I know that I shall not be ashamed*} Or, *blush:* which comes near to the Hebrew term here used; in notion the same with the former. See, Psalm 25:2,3 & 119:6, chapter 29:22.

**V. 8.** *{He is near, that justifieth me*} God is ready to justify me, by approving my mission, and his acceptance of my employments, against those that oppose my ministry, and traduce me, as a false prophet, as many did Paul, for a counterfeit apostle, 1 Corinthians 4:2,3, 2 Corinthians 13:6,7, for so the word, much mistaken by many, does there properly signify. This some understand of Christ, according to those places, John 16:10, 1 Timothy 3:16. See chapter 49:4. Others, because of the apostle's, either allegation, or allusion rather, to it, Romans 8:33,34, understand it, as spoken in the person of God's people in general; as chapter 29:22 & 41:10–14 & 45:24,25 & 46:13 and 49:25 & 54:19, where the same things, in effect, here spoken, are applied unto the body of that people. But the apostle's manner is, to enlarge the promises of God, made to some particular persons, as to Jacob, Joshua, David, and others, Genesis 28:15, Joshua 1:5, Psalm 23:1, extending them unto all the faithful in general, as having a joint interest therein with them, Hebrews 13:5,6, and the apostle's argument, borrowed hence, stands firm and good, in general, that whom God justifies, it is in vain for any man to attaint, or condemn.

*{who will contend with me?*} Enter plea against me, or implead me, chapter 49:25 & 54:17.

*{let us stand together:*} As the accuser, or plaintiff, and the defendant, such as have suits in law, one with another, are wont to do before the judge, Exodus 22:9, Deuteronomy 19:17.

*{who is mine adversary?*} As some render it *the master,* or, *owner of my cause,* or, *of my judgment:* but rather, *my master,* or, *owner of suit: judgment,* for, *cause,* or lawsuit, as, 2 Chronicles 6:35, Job 9:19, and *master,* or *owner of suit,* for one that *sues;* as *master* or *owner of business,* for, one that *hath business,* Exodus 24:14, and, *my master,* or *owner of suit,* for, one that has any suit against me: my impleader, or he that enters any action against me; so, *thy men men of strife,* for, *they that strive with thee,* chapter 41:11.

*{let him come near to me.*} Let him join issue with me; as chapter 41:1.

**V. 9.** *{Behold, the Lord God will help me:*} As verse 7.

*{who is he, that shall condemn me?*} Or, *who is it, that shall,* or, *can condemn me?* Hebrew, *make me guilty,* convince, or condemn me, as guilty, Deuteronomy 25:1, Proverbs 17:15, Romans 8:34, the pronoun, for the verb substantive, as Ecclesiastes 1:10, chapter 50:1, the relative wanting, as 49:25, and the future in a potential notion, as verse 3.

*{Lo, they shall all wax old as a garment;*} All my opposites shall be worn out; I shall survive to outwear them, to see an end of them, a proverbial form of speech, Psalm 120:26, chapter 51:6, Hebrews 1:11, a *garment* for an old or overworn *garment,* such, as Joshua 9:4,5, Jeremiah 38:11, or a moth-eaten *garment;* as the next clause implies, a defect of the adjunct, as chapter 1:18 & 5:6. *wax old,* that is, be *consumed,* or *wasted,* as Psalm 32:3, or, *perish;* as it is expounded, Psalm 102:26. So chapter 41:11, *those that contend with thee, shall perish.*

*{the moth shall eat them up*} Another proverbial form, Psalm 39:11, chapter 51:8.

**V. 10.** *{Who is among you that feareth the Lord,*} He turns his speech from those obstinate, and opposite ones, to the pious and obedient; as endeavoring to support and sustain them amidst the common calamities, that were to befall the nation: so withal implying the small number of such among them. So Psalm 25:12 & 90:11, chapter 53:1, John 12:37,38.

*{that obeyeth the voice of his servant,*} Hebrew, *that heareth:* but *to hear,* for *to obey.* See on verse 4. That yields obedience to the word of his servant; Christ, as some, chapter 42:1 & 53:11, speaking either by himself, Luke 4:18,21,22, Hebrews 1:1,2. Or, by his ministers, Luke 10:16, 2 Corinthians 5:20 and 13:3, Ephesians 2:17. Or, as others, the prophet Esay himself, sent by God, to inform, and instruct, his people, and to acquaint them with his will, chapter 44:26. A note of one that sincerely fears God, as to tremble at his word, chapter 66:2, so to yield obedience thereunto, Ecclesiastes 12:13.

*{that walketh in darkness, and hath no light?*} Hebrew, *no shine,* as Amos 5:20, no light shining (as Proverbs 4:18.) upon him, or into him; as a man in a dungeon, where no glimpse of light strikes in, *to walk in darkness,* is sometime to live in wickedness, 1 John 1:6, and so the Jewish commenters, some of them, here understand it; as if it were said, you that walk in blind paths, and take wicked courses, return to God, and trust in him: sometime to live in misery and distress, Psalm 23:4, and so rather here; as other of them also much better and most of the best with us; that is, in the greatest depth of misery and calamity that may be, without any means of relief or comfort. So are *light* and *darkness* oft taken, Psalm 18:28 and 112:4, chapter 9:1,2. See chapter 8:22 & 9:19, Amos 5:18. Some observing the Hebrew pauses, end the demand at the foregoing branch, where the middling stop stands in the original; and joining this limb to the next following, read the words thus; *Let him that walketh in darkness, having no light, trust in the Lord.* Or, *he that walketh in darkness,* etc. *let him trust in the Lord;* which comes all to one; Let such as you, or so many of you, as are in straits and difficulties, as well as others, partaking with the rest, in the common calamities of the times.

*{let him trust in the name of the Lord*} Let him live by faith and sustain himself by confidence in, and assurance of, God's powerful protection; who is able to draw light out of darkness, to give light in darkness, to turn darkness into light, and to bring out of darkness into the light; to give inward joy and comfort amidst all calamities, to support and sustain under all heavy pressures, and to deliver out of all distresses, Genesis 1:2,3, Exodus 10:22,23, Esther 3:15 & 4:3 & 8:16,17, Psalm 1828. 11.2,4,7, chapter 9:2 & 49:9 & .2, Luke 1:79.60, 2 Corinthians 4:6. See 1 Samuel 30:6, Habakkuk 2:4 & 3:17,18, Hebrews 10:38.

*{and stay upon his God*} As a man stays up himself with a staff, that he rests upon for support, Psalm 18:18 & 23:4, chapter 10:20, (for thence is the metaphor taken. See chapter 3:1 & 36:6.) so let him rely, and rest himself upon his God, whom he cleaves close, and continues loyal unto, (Deuteronomy 4:3,4 & 26:17,19, chapter 28:16, Psalm 73:25–28.) by constant dependence upon him, staying up, and supporting himself from sinking down, and fainting away through incredulity and despair, Psalm 27:13. So may such, and such only, boldly do, their expectation never failing them, Psalm 125:1,2, chapter 28:16 & 49:23, their sincere confidence in God being here opposed, as well to the folly and vanity of those that withdraw themselves from God, and trust to other stays, Jeremiah 17:5,6, Jonah 2:8, verse 11, as also to the groundless presumption of such, as promise to themselves protection and safeguard from him, while they carry themselves disloyally, and rebelliously towards him, chapter 48:1,2, Jeremiah 7:8–10.

**V. 11.** *{Behold all ye that kindle a fire,*} The expositions of this passage, are so numerous, and so various, that it would be overlong to relate, and much more to discuss them all. I will pitch only upon one or two of the principal, and most probable. By the *fire* therefore here mentioned, some understand the fire of God's wrath, which wicked persons, and obstinate wretches, do incense against themselves by their sins. So some of the Jewish commenters, and most of ours also, pointing us to those places, Deuteronomy 32:22, Jeremiah 5:14 & 17:4. But others, rather, understand by it such other means of light, support, relief, and comfort, as the wicked worldlings of those times that relied upon, for their succor and safeguard, in, and against those evils and calamities, that were denounced against them and the state, by the prophet. See chapter 28:15 & 30:7,12,15,16, for to these, the prophet's opposites, that scorned God's word, and refused to hear it, or yield obedience unto it, chapter 28:13,14 & 30:9,12, does the prophet here direct his speech. So in the word, here, is an allusion, not to such a fire, as burns and consumes; as chapter 9:18 & 26:11, but to such a fire, as men kindle in cold, wet, and winter weather, to warm, relieve, comfort, and cherish themselves with, chapter 44:16, Jeremiah 36:22, John 18:18, Acts 28:2. See the like allusion, chapter 47:14.

*{that compass yourselves about, with sparks*} Hebrew, *girders on of sparks* or *brands:* that *begirt* yourselves with such; as some are said to *gird on strength,* or to begirt themselves with *strength,* 1 Samuel 2:4. Most render the word, here used, *sparks,* and suppose an allusion to such sparklings, as upon collision of steel and stone, are wont to start out, or, to such sparkles as are wont to fly about folk, upon the blowing up of brands: no unfit resemblance of such, as by their rebellious provocation, so incense and blow up the fire of God's wrath, that the sparks fly about their ears. See chapter 42:24,25, and this way may that seem to incline, that in Chaldee, and Syriac, a word from this deduced, is deemed to signify, *sparks,* in the paraphrase, on Exodus 24:18, and on Habakkuk 3:4, in which latter place, yet it seems rather to import such *coruscations,* or *flashes of light,* as use to shoot out of the clouds, somewhat like unto *horns,* for so the Hebrew word there used signifies, as also a Greek and Latin, correspondent thereunto, whence some ambiguous versions, and fabulous constructions of them, Exodus 34:29. But to let that pass, the word itself here used seems rather to signify *brands,* than *sparks:* It is nowhere else found in Scripture, save here, and Proverbs 26:18, where it is well rendered in the text, *firebrands,* not so well in the margin *flames,* or *sparks;* for such as *play the madmen,* or *make themselves mad,* (that is, *feign themselves* such; as *make thyself sick,* that is, *feign thyself* to be so, 2 Samuel 13:5, for of such the wise man there speaks) are not wont to fling *flame,* and *sparks,* but to cast *firebrands* about. And the Chaldee there renders it, *torches,* or *tapers;* as also one of the Jewish critics upon this place informs us, that the term is used for such parcels of wood, or coal, as being fired at one end, were out of engines discharged in fight against the enemy, or shot into places besieged; the use of guns, and gunpowder being in his times, and long after, in these parts of the world, at least unknown. And it seems therefore to be a term parallel to that other elsewhere used, that signifies, *a firebrand,* Judges 15:4, Amos 4:11. Those shifts, therefore, and fetches, which these profane wretches relied upon, and from whence they promised sufficient warmth of relief, comfort, yea, and safety to themselves, being on every side therewith begirt, the prophet compares unto *brands,* that should afford them little heat, or light, but smoke enough, to vex and choke them with. See chapter 7:4.

*{walk in the light of your fire, and of the sparks, which ye have kindled*} *Brands* here again, not *sparks:* for men use not to kindle sparks, though upon kindling of fire sparks in brands, especially, are wont to fly about. Some, because the former word here used, is sometime used for a *furnace,* or a *flame.* (See chapter 31:9.) would have it rendered, *Go into the furnace,* or *flame of the fire, ye have kindled;* as foretelling, that thereby they should be consumed, to wit, by the fire of God's wrath, which themselves had kindled, and heated, as an oven, to consume themselves, Psalm 21:9. But I suppose rather that the prophet, in way of derision, wills them to make trial, when time shall be and need require, what light of comfort their own fire, with all the muster of brands kindled by them, and set about them, will be able to afford them. See verse 10. No, the light of the wicked shall be put out in darkness, and go away in a stifling stench, Job 18:5,6 & 21:17, Proverbs 20:20 & 24:20, a defect of the relative, as chapter 49:25.

*{This shall ye have of mine hand*} This take from me God's messenger, that now speak unto you; hand, for *ministry;* as Malachi 1:1. Or, as most take it, spoken in the person of God which some therefore read as in the present tense, *This is unto you from mine hand,* that is, this obcecation of mind, and obduration of heart, is, through my just judgment, for your former obstinacy, befallen you, chapter 6:10 & 29:10, Matthew 13:14. But others, rather, in the future, as our version gives it, this that I now tell you, shall, in conclusion, befall you, whatsoever you now fondly flatter yourselves with, chapter 28:15,17,18.

*{ye shall lie down in sorrow*} You that have refused to walk in the light of God's favor, Psalm 89:15, and in obedience to his word that holy fire, that affords both light and heat, Psalm 119:105,92,93, Luke 24:32, John 12:35,36, shall, notwithstanding all the fire that you kindle, and vain lights that you set up for yourselves, wander in the dark, and meet with nothing but perplexity and confusion in the end, Psalm 16:4, chapter 8:21,22 & 28:19 & 30:12–14, Jeremy 13:16.

*{lie down in sorrow*} A metaphor from an uneasy bed, whereon, one that made account to ease and refresh himself, finds nothing but disease and pain, and is in worse case, by reason of the uneasiness of it, than he was before he betook himself to it, Job 7:3,4,13–15, chapter 28:19,20. Or, to bedclothes, wherein a man lies enfolded, and wrapped up over head and ears. So Jeremiah 3:25, *we lie down in our shame, and our confusion covereth us,* and 1 John 5:19, *the whole world lieth down in evil.* Howbeit, some, both of the Jewish commenters, and others, conceive in it, an intimation of death and destruction; because of *decease* the word is oft used, Genesis 47:30, 1 Kings 20:10, Job 7:21, chapter 14:8.

### CHAPTER 51

**V. 1.** *{Hearken to me ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the Lord*} The prophet returns here, to comfort and encourage the godly party again, endeavor to keep them from being dismayed, and discouraged, either by the consideration of their own fewness and feebleness, verse 2,3, or by the apprehension of the supposed might, together with the joint malice, and multitude of the adverse party, verse 4–8.

*{Hearken to me*} As chapter 41:1 & 44:1 & 49:1.

*{ye that follow after righteousness*} Hebrew, *pursuers of righteousness,* as, *pursuers of mischief,* Psalm 119:150, that continue constant in the serious and sedulous practice of holiness, and righteousness, Proverbs 21:21. Or, as some, that seek righteousness by faith in Christ, Romans 9:31,32, but the former here rather, as also, chapter 56:1,2, Matthew 5:20 & 6:33. There seems in the phrase a metaphor, either from a worldly man's eagerness, in following the world, in some gainful trade, whereof, he never has enough, Ecclesiastes 5:10. Or, the instancy of huntsmen, or military persons, in pursuit of their foe, or prey, 2 Samuel 2:19. So Psalm 37:15, chapter 1:22, Hebrews 12:14.

*{that seek the Lord*} The character of a true Israelite, Psalm 24:6. See chapter 55:6, Zephaniah 2:3.

*{look unto the rock, whence ye are hewn*} Or, *were hewn,* rather. Abraham and Sarah, from whom, they came, as stones cut out of a rock, or digged out of a quarry; Daniel 2:34. Some would have Abraham here termed a *rock,* as a dead, and dry, rocky substance, unfit to yield issue, Romans 4:19. Others, for the firmness of his faith, Genesis 15:6, Romans 4:3,18–22, as Peter was a *rock,* or a *stone,* Matthew 10:2 & 16:18, John 1:42. Neither seems necessary, and the latter of the twain the less: as not seeming at all, in this resemblance, to be regarded: Since that it is not the firmness of Abraham's faith, that is here propounded for imitation, but the bareness, and barrenness of him, and his wife, in regard of issue, and the improbability, yea, in human apprehension, impossibility, of attaining to any increase in that kind; such much less, as afterward issued from them: not what Abraham upon God's word believed, but what God did for Abraham, verse 2.

*{and to the hole of the pit, whence ye were digged*} Or, *to the hollow of the cistern: whence ye were digged,* Jeremiah 2:13, to Sarah, and to her womb, deemed as dead, and utterly disabled unto issue, Genesis 11:30 & 16:1 & 18:11,12, Romans 4:19, (for from the word here used, has a *woman* her name in Hebrew; and to a *well,* or *cistern,* is the wife compared, Proverbs 5:15.) until God, beyond the course, or power of nature, opened her womb, as he did that hollow place in Lehi, Judges 15:19, and gave her power to conceive issue, Hebrews 11:11. There is a want of the relative, either pronoun, or adverb, as well in this branch as in the former also.

**V. 2.** *{Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah, that bare you*} The explication of the former words, in plainer terms: a want again of the relative; in the latter branch; as chapter 50:11.

*{Abraham*} The name then given him, when a large issue was promised him; at which time, with an enlargement, he was by God himself, so named; as *the father of a great multitude:* whereas he was called *Avram* only, as *an high,* or *lofty father,* before, Genesis 17:5.

*{your father*} Theirs in a more special manner, because descended from him, both by Isaac, in whom his seed was to be reckoned, Genesis 17:21 & 21:12, and by Jacob, to whom the birthright, and blessing was devolved from Esau, Genesis 25:33,34 & 27:29,30,33,35,36, and was, through him, derived unto all his posterity, Genesis 49, Exodus 24:4 & 27:11,21, Deuteronomy 33. Otherwise, there were divers nations also besides the Israelites, of the lineage of Abraham; as the Ismaelites, the Edomites, and others. See Genesis 17:20 & 21:13 and 25:2–4,12–18 and 36, and of him, therefore, as more peculiarly their father, did the Jews much vaunt, Mark 3:9, John 8:33,39.

*{Sarah*} The name likewise given her, at the same time with Abraham's; signifying a *lady,* or *princess,* without limitation, or restriction, at large: whereas she was formerly termed *Sarai,* signifying *my lady,* or *my princess,* as with a relation to Abram, her husband, and *lord,* or *prince,* alone: for the one title she gave him, Genesis 18:12, 1 Peter 3:6, and the Hethites, the other, Genesis 23:6, her ladyship, or princessdom, being now to be enlarged, Genesis 17:15,16.

*{that bare you*} The word implies the pain of breeding, and birth; in Rebecca more remarkable, Genesis 25:22, the same word is found, Psalm 51:55, that *bare you;* not immediately but mediately, in Isaac to Abraham, Genesis 17:21, a defect of the relative, as before verse 1, chapter 47:11.

*{for I called him alone*} Or, *how I called him alone:* as the particle is used, Exodus 19:4, Psalm 119:159, chapter 66:24, Lamentations 1:9. Or, *how, when, he was but one, I called him,* Hebrew, *when one, I called him: one,* for, one only, or, but *one,* as Deuteronomy 6:4, Zechariah 14:9, *one* only, or, *a lone man:* because though married, yet childless; and in regard of issue, as wifeless: she being barren, and aged, in course of nature past childing, and not without issue only, but past hope of any by her, Genesis 15:2 & 16:1. See Ezekiel 33:24, and above, on verse 1.

*{and blessed him, and increased him,*} God's blessing is no verbal, but a real blessing: the bestowing of a blessing. So Genesis 1:28 and 9:1, and this blessing of multiplication, and increase, was more specially though, among many other blessings, conferred upon Abraham, Genesis 12:2,3 & 15:5 & 17:2 & 18:18 & 22:17,18, here pointed to, as picked out of the whole heap; to strengthen the faith of God's people, against the conceit and apprehension of their paucity, and imbecility, by setting before their eyes, a pregnant pattern of God's power, able to raise up, of one, and that one, not a decayed only, but, in some sort, as a dead one, an issue for multitude, like the stars of the sky, and sands of the sea, beyond number, Hebrews 11:12, and no less able, therefore, to do the like also for them. See chapter 49:19–21, Jeremiah 31:27, Ezekiel 37:11–14,26.

**V. 3.** *{For the Lord shall comfort Zion, he will comfort all her waste places*} God can do, and will do as much for his church, as he sometime did for Abraham.

*{shall comfort Zion*} Or, *will;* as in the next branch.

*{comfort Zion*} He will comfort his people; (so is Zion taken, chapter 1:27 & 49:14.) not by speaking only comfortably to them, chapter 40:1, Hosea 2:14, but by relieving, and refreshing of them, chapter 12:1 & 49:13 & 54:9.

*{he will comfort all her waste places*} Or, *wastes,* chapter 49:19. By restoring the ruined city, and state, to her wonted beauty and luster again, chapter 49:8 & 54:3 & 58:11.

*{and he will make her wilderness like Eden*} He will raise her up to a flourishing estate, and make her land, as pleasant and plentiful, as paradise; called *Eden,* for the daintiness and delightfulness of it, Genesis 2:8,9 & 13:10, Ezekiel 36:35. See on chapter 4:2 and 35:1.

*{and her desert*} Or, *champaign,* as Joshua 11:2 & 12:3.

*{like the garden of the Lord*} *As a garden of God:* that is, a most excellent one: as *mountains of God,* for, goodly great mountains, Psalm 36:6, and *cedars of God,* for, goodly tall cedars, Psalm 104:16, and, *an host of God,* for, a mighty great host, 1 Chronicles 12:22. Or, *as the garden of Eden.* (The same thing in other terms,) so called, Genesis 13:10, Ezekiel 28:13, because of God's own planting, Genesis 2:8. See chapter 60:21 & 61:3.

*{joy and gladness shall be found therein; thanksgiving and the voice of melody*} So Jeremiah 33:11. See chapter 35:10.

*{shall be found there*} Or, *shall be there:* as Esther 1:5, chapter 35:9.

**V. 4.** *{Hearken unto me, O my people; and give ear unto me, O my nation*} My peculiar people, whom, from all other nations, I have set apart, and singled out for myself, Exodus 19:5, Deuteronomy 7:6. See chapter 28:23 & 44:1.

*{for a law shall proceed from me*} As a law sometime proceeded from me in Mount Sinai, Deuteronomy 33:2, so a second law, in the doctrine of the gospel, not for the restitution of my church, among you only, but for the information, and direction of other people also, shall hereafter go abroad from me, chapter 2:3, Psalm 110:2.

*{and I will make my judgment to rest for a light of the people.*} The *judgment,* here spoken of, is no other, than the law, or, doctrine before mentioned. For, *law, doctrine, judgment, word, precept, statute,* are words promiscuously used oft one for another. See Psalm 19:7,8,9 and Psalm 119 throughout.

*{make to rest*} So some render it, that is, *I will settle it,* there; to wit, in my church: because the word signifies sometime *to rest,* chapter 34:14, Jeremiah 50:34. Others, *I will suddenly execute my judgment.* I will speedily do, what I now speak: because this stock has oftentimes a notion of *suddenness,* Jeremiah 4:20 & 18:7, see verse 5, and others again, because it signifies sometime *to break:* as Job 7:5, render it, *I will cause my judgment,* that is, my doctrine, *to break forth;* as light is said *to break out.* See Psalm 119:130, Hosea 6:5, and though this seem not altogether improbable, yet because that use of the word seems not so clear, I go rather with the first. For the Jewish doctors here seem to run counter to the text; as if the meaning were, that God would cause his people to rest a while, while he executed judgment upon the Gentiles; as chapter 26:20, Jeremiah 50:34.

*{for the light of the people*} Hebrew, *peoples:* as Psalm 117:1, to enlighten their minds with the saving knowledge of God's truth, Psalm 19:7,8 & 119:105,130, Proverbs 6:23, 2 Corinthians 4:6, Revelation 1:20. See chapter 49:6.

**V. 5.** *{My righteousness is near*} The time approaches, of accomplishing my promise, in the deliverance of my people, chapter 1:27 and 48:13 and 56:1, an effect of my faithfulness, and righteousness, 1 Thessalonians 5:24, 2 Thessalonians 1:6,7, Hebrews 6:9,10, 1 John 1:9. See chapter 13:22. They force it overmuch, that would have it, *my righteousness;* that is, *my righteous one:* applying it to Cyrus; as most do, as forcedly expounding the like of Abraham, chapter 41:2.

*{my salvation is gone forth*} The decree is gone out for my people's deliverance, which shall speedily be accomplished either as having respect unto God's purpose revealed unto the prophet, and by him to his people, chapter 14:24–27. Or, to Cyrus his edict, as ready to go out, or gone out already, Ezra 1:1,2. See chapter 13:22 and 43:19.

*{and mine arms shall judge the people:*} Hebrew, *peoples;* as verse 4. *Arms,* in the plural, to intimate the greatness of God's power, and the large extent of the exercise thereof; either in the subduing and taking vengeance of those that had been enemies to his church, and oppressors of his people, chapter 25:10,11,12 and 32:2–8 and 49:25,26. Or, in the managing of his church, and the nations, out of all parts gathered into it, chapter 2:4. See chapter 59:16.

*{the isles shall wait upon me*} Or, *lands, countries;* even those about, and beyond the sea: as chapter 49:1. See chapter 42:4 and 60:9.

*{and on mine arm shall they trust*} On his power and might, manifested, in the execution of judgment upon the enemies of his people, and in the rescuing of them, out of their hands, chapter 52:10 & 59:16,19, Psalm 98:1,2. Or, on his word, and gospel, by which, having subdued them, and brought them in to himself, he shall, also, as by his mighty arm, and powerful scepter, rule and reign, in the midst of them, chapter 53:1, Psalm 110:2, Ezekiel 20:33,34, Romans 1:16, 1 Corinthians 1:16.

**V. 6.** *{Lift up your eyes to the heavens: and look upon the earth beneath*} Consider how firm and stable they seem to be. See chapter 40:26, Psalm 24:2 & 93:1 & 104:5.

*{for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke*} Hebrew, *be dissolved* or *melted, as salt;* so the word properly signifies. See Jeremiah 38:11, and so does a late learned writer expound the Greek word precisely answering it, Mark 9:49, *every sacrifice shall be wasted,* or *consumed with fire* and so pass into smoke, Psalm 37:20, chapter 34:4, Matthew 24:35, 2 Peter 3:10, Revelation 6:14.

*{and the earth shall wax old like a garment*} Psalm 102:26, Hebrews 1:11, Mark 13:31. See chapter 50:9, verse 8.

*{and they that dwell therein*} Or, *thereon;* as Matthew 6:30. Hebrew, *her inhabitants.*

*{shall die in like manner*} Joshua 23:14, 1 Kings 2:2, Job 14:1,2, Psalm 89:48, Hebrews 9:27.

*{in like manner*} That is, as smoke, or old rotten rags, the matters before mentioned: so interpreters, generally; taking the term here used, for a note of similitude: as usually it is, Psalm 1:4, chapter 16:6. But a late learned annotator renders it, *as a louse;* taking it for a noun, (for a note of similitude there is here besides) whose plural is, found, Exodus 8:16,17,18, and the words of the text do not only well bear it, but seem even to require it. See somewhat the like, Psalm 39:11, *as a louse,* for, as any sorry despicable vermin.

*{but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished*} Though heaven and earth fail, yet shall not my promises fail, nor the salvation therein promised; those shall sooner fail, and have an end, than these shall, Psalm 119:89,90, chapter 45:17 & 50:9 & 54:10, Matthew 5:18, Mark 13:31, John 3:16, Hebrews 12:28.

**V. 7.** *{Hearken unto me*} As verse 1.

*{ye that know righteousness*} Not only that know it, and what belongs to it, but that approve, regard, and make reckoning of it. So is the word of *knowing,* frequently used, Psalm 1:6, Proverbs 12:10, Matthew 7:23, Romans 7:15. See verse 1.

*{the people in whose heart is my law,*} That highly esteem of it, and heartily affect it; having it not in the head only, but in the heart also, Psalm 37:31 and 40:8 & 119:97,103,111,112,113,127,128.

*{fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings.*} See chapter 8:12 & 41:10–14, Matthew 10:28, Luke 12:3,4, Acts 5:40,41.

*{men*} Hebrew, *man,* or mortal, miserable *men.* See on chapter 2:9.

*{afraid*} Rather *terrified, affrighted, damped, disheartened,* chapter 31:9, Jeremiah 10:1.

*{of their revilings*} Or, *with their spiteful taunts:* for so the word seems to import, chapter 37:6,23, Psalm 44:16.

**V. 8.** *{For the moth shall eat them up like a garment,*} A proverbial speech. See chapter 50:9, Job 13:28, Psalm 39:11.

*{and the worm shall eat them up like wool.*} Another proverbial form of speech; for notion, one with the former: *wool,* for a woolen garment, more prone to breed mites and moths, than linen.

*{but my righteousness shall be forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.*} Hebrew, *to generation of generations,* as Psalm 102:24. See on verse 6.

**V. 9.** *{Awake, awake,*} This is spoken either in the person of God's people, or by the prophet himself, moving in their behalf.

*{Awake, awake,*} Or, *Arise, arise;* raise and rouse up yourself, so, verse 17, chapter 52:1. So also Jeremiah 6:22 & 25:32, because the term of *awaking,* seems not to suit so well with the *arm.* Yet according to the like, of *tongue, lute,* and *harp,* Psalm 56:8 & 108:3, it may be retained, and the sense of it applied unto God; whose *arm* is his power, and his power the same with himself. Manifest yourself to be awake, and to watch for us, and over us, Psalm 121:3,4, and that in a powerful manner; who, at present, by suffering us to lie in misery, under heavy pressures, may seem to be asleep, and not at all to regard us, or look after us. So Psalm 44:23 and 78:65 and 80:2. The redoubling of the word, intimates the vehemency of their affection, and earnest desire of speedy relief and release. See the like, Judges 5:12, chapter 52:1, so Psalm 13:1 & 94:3.

*{put on strength*} Show forth your might, in that manner, by succoring and saving of us, that it may evidently appear, and as conspicuously be seen, as a man's garment is on him, that wears it. See chapter 52:1 & 59:17 & 61:10, so Psalm 93:1 & 98:1,2,3,5 & 40:5.

*{O arm of the Lord*} See verse 5, chapter 52:10.

*{awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old*} Arise, and bestir yourself, as in former times you have done, Psalm 44:1, chapter 63:11–14. Hebrew, *in days of antiquity* (as chapter 37:26.) *generations of ages,* as *years of ages,* Psalm 77:5.

*{Art not thou it that hath cut Rahab*} Or, *that did cut,* or *hew Rahab:* that by *Rahab* is meant *Egypt,* so far as I know, no doubt is made. But how Egypt came to be so termed, is not altogether so generally agreed. Most are of opinion, that from her *pride,* and *power* pretended, at least, (chapter 30:2,3,7.) that name was given her. See Ezekiel 30:6, and the word may well import, either. See Job 9:13, Psalm 90:13. Howbeit, a learned author conceives Egypt to be so termed, from the figure, or form, of the lower part of that country; which the river Nilus, having with one entire stream attained unto, does at the head thereof, where it is sharpest and narrowest, divide itself into two main channels; and so shooting down on either side of the land, growing wider and wider, encloses it in that manner, till it arrive at the sea, that it makes it to be of a pyramidal, or triangular form, with the point upward, and the basis beneath, to the seaward. Hence the Greek term this part of Egypt, *Delta,* because it had the shape of their *D.* thus drawn Δ, and the Egyptians themselves called it *Riph,* or *Rib,* by a word that signifies *a pear,* the fashion whereof it bore: whence the head city of the middlemost canton, within that land, was named *Athribæs;* which signifies, the heart of *a pear,* and some late authors, also, make mention of the name *Errif,* with the Arabic article prefixed. *Rib* and *Rahab* therefore he holds to be all one; as *Nahal,* and *Nilus.* And these things, indeed, carry some good show of probability with them. Howbeit, it may be doubted, whether this *Rif,* or *Rib,* for *a pear,* be an homebred Egyptian word or no. For it may not, without some good ground, be suspected, that as the Arabian *Phil,* or *Pil,* and with their article *Elphil,* for an *elephant,* sprung, as most learned deem, either from the Hebrew *Eleph,* for an *ox,* or the Greeks and Latins, *Elephas,* recised and reversed; so that this Egyptian *Rib,* or *Riph,* for *a pear,* was taken from the Latin *Pyrum,* the Latin termination being cut off, and the term itself inverted; that which the rather may be supposed, because in those pieces of the Egyptian language, which learned men have of late acquainted us with, words, as well Latin, as Greek, are found not a few. And the Arabian *Errif,* may more justly be deemed to descend from the Hebrew *Rahab,* than the Hebrew *Rahab* to have flown from it, as *Nilus,* from *Nahal,* not *Nahal* from it. I should therefore rather incline to the received notation of this name, given unto Egypt, being a proud and potent state, from a ready Hebrew original; than to one so far fetched about, from grounds, neither of any great certainty, nor of approved antiquity; and appliable, in comparison, but to a small part of the country.

*{and wounded the dragon*} Or, *didst thrust through,* (as the word properly signifies. See chapter 2:19 and 5:12.) Or, *slay,* (as it is well rendered, Ezekiel 28:9 and 32:26, and would also be here) *the whale.* (See chapter 27:1.) Pharao, Psalm 74:14, so termed, in regard of the streams of the river Nilus, amidst which, his abode was, and the neighborhood of the sea. See Ezekiel 29:13 & 32:2.

**V. 10.** *{Art not thou it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep?*} Or, *which did dry the sea:* as before, verse 9, the Red Sea, Exodus 14:21, chapter 50:2.

*{that hath made the depth of the sea, a way for the ransomed to pass over?*} Or, *didst make the deeps* or *deep places* (as *wastes,* for waste places, verse 3, so also, Psalm 69:2.) *of the sea, a way for the rescued ones;* (as Psalm 107:2, those that he not only delivered out of Egypt; but rescued also from the hand of Pharao, who pursued them with the sword, and was ready to seize upon them, Exodus 14:10–13 & 15:9.) *to pass by,* or *pass through,* Exodus 14:22, chapter 43:16 & 63:11–13.

**V. 11.** *{Therefore the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing unto Zion*} Or, *So,* in like manner. Hebrew, *And;* but so also is the copulative oft used, Proverbs 26:7, chapter 41:7.) *the Lord's rescued ones shall come again unto Sion, with song.* See chapter 35:10, those that shall be delivered from the Babylonian captivity; God being able to do as much for these now, as he did for those then, chapter 43:16 & 44:27 & 50:2.

*{and everlasting joy shall be upon their head?*} Or, *with song, and everlasting joy upon their head.* So it was rendered, chapter 35:10. See chapter 43:20.

*{they shall attain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away*} See chapter 35:10, it is all of it, God's answer to the former supplication, in way of an humble expostulation propounded, verse 7,8.

**V. 12.** *{I, even I, am he that comforteth you*} See verse 2. The word is, for the greater emphasis, redoubled; as chapter 43:25.

*{who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die; and of the son of man, that shall be made as grass?*} A secret reproof of them, that having the immortal, and almighty God, to their protector and Savior, should be afraid of a frail mortal man, chapter 2:22, Matthew 10:28, verse 7,8.

*{that thou shouldest fear*} Hebrew, *and thou shalt fear.* See the like syntax, Genesis 23:19, Joshua 24:7, chapter 53:2.

*{man, and son of man*} As Job 25:6, Psalm 8:4.

*{that shall die*} As verse 6, Psalm 118:6 and 146:4, a defect of the relative, both here, and in the next branch; as also, chapter 50:9.

*{shall be made as grass*} Or, *shall become grass,* or *made like hay:* but there is an emphasis, in the omission of the note of similitudes, as chapter 40:6, Psalm 27:3 and 90:5,6. Hebrew, *shall be given grass,* or *hay:* but the word of *giving,* signifies oftentimes *to make,* Numbers 14:4, Nehemiah 13:26, Jeremiah 9:14, and, *to be made,* for *to become.*

**V. 13.** *{And forgettest the Lord thy maker*} Consider not his power and what he is able to do for you: *to forget,* for *not to consider;* as Hebrews 12:5. See chapter 40:27–29.

*{thy maker*} Chapter 44:2, Hosea 8:14.

*{that hath stretched out the heaven*} Chapter 42:5 and 45:12.

*{and hath laid the foundations of the earth*} Chapter 48:13, Job 38:4, Psalm 102:25.

*{and hast feared continually every day*} Or, *all the day long,* as Psalm 44:22, Romans 8:36, were never free from fear; but lived in a perpetual expectation of death, Hebrews 2:15, notwithstanding the assurance given you, by God, of his constant protection, chapter 43:1,2.

*{because of the fury of the oppressor, as if he were ready to destroy;*} Or, *had made himself ready to destroy;* and there were no possibility of escape: So Genesis 19:19,30, Exodus 14:10–12.

*{and where is the fury of the oppressor?*} What is now become of the fury of the Babylonians your oppressors, whose fury you stood so much in fear of? They are perished, and it is gone, Psalm 9:5,6 & 76:10, chapter 16:4.

**V. 14.** *{The captive exile hasteneth that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail*} Or, *The exile* (he that is *gone,* to wit, out of his country, as Jeremiah 48:12, for the word *captive,* is not in the original) *is hastening to be loosed.* (Hebrew, *to be opened;* as chapter 15:17, Job 12:18 & 39:5, that have the prison door opened to him, and to be set free from his bonds and restraint; *is hastening to be loosed,* for *shall hastily,* or *speedily be loosed.* So Genesis 41:32, *God is making haste to do it,* that is, will do it speedily, out of hand.) *and he shall not die in the pit,* (but shall be timely released) *nor shall his bread fail,* as in sieges, and such restraint, it oft does. See Jeremiah 37:22 & 38:9,10, that which some apply here to that spiritual food, John 6:27. See chapter 33:16. The meaning is: My people, that are at present driven out of their own country, and clapped up in holes and dungeons, chapter 42:22, shall be speedily set at liberty; Nor shall they perish in their prisons, and places of restraint, for want of food, by delay; nor in their journeying home again, through want of victuals, by the way. See chapter 49:9,10. Yet I cannot omit, that some here read the words, *He* (to wit, the *oppressor,* that now holds you in bondage, verse 13.) *shall hasten,* (that is, *hastily bring out,* as 1 Kings 22:9.) *the exile that is to be loosed.* Or, as with an allusion to the Egyptian deliverance, *He hasteneth,* or *shall make haste,* the oppressor going to and fro, or *running up and down,* (so the word seems to be taken, chapter 63:1, Jeremiah 2:20.) *to set at liberty;* and so it is said of the Egyptians, that God said, that Pharao and his followers should (as also accordingly they did) come to Moses, and to his people, and instantly press them to be gone from among them, Exodus 11:8 and 12:31–33, and so the meaning should be, that God would enforce the Babylonians to do the like by them. But this seems not to flow so freely from the text, as the former.

*{in the pit*} That is, *in the hole,* or *the dungeon,* as chapter 42:22, Zechariah 9:2, but the word, here used, is applied commonly to the grave, Job 33:18,24,33, Psalm 30:9 & 55:23, the rather here made use of, because the place of their captivity, seemed to be unto them, as a *grave* and the getting out of the one, as impossible, as the rising from the other, chapter 26:19, Ezekiel 37:11,12.

**V. 15.** *{For I am the Lord thy God, that divided the sea, whose waves roared*} Hebrew, *And;* as chapter 40:26. Or, *I the Lord thy God, am he, that divided the sea, when his waves roared;* and so read, it should have reference to that of the Red Sea; before spoken of, verse 10, which being effected, by a stiff and strong blast of wind; beating back the current of it, Exodus 14:12, could not be done, say those, that so render it, but with an hideous roaring noise: But I find not where the word here used does signify, *to divide,* save, as any thing, that is cracked or broken, may be said to be divided: and so Job says, Job 7:5, *my skin cracketh,* or *breaketh:* and of the sea, it is said, Job 26:12, *By his power he breaketh the sea;* as it is commonly rendered: where interpreters dispute much what should be meant by *breaking of the sea:* For it cannot be there understood of the dividing of the Red Sea: it being generally agreed, that Job was ancienter than those times: and the most therefore understand it, of *troubling* the sea, and setting it on working, as Psalm 107:25, Jonah 1:4,13, and so, also, both the ancient Greek, and the old Latin, here render it, reading the words, *that trouble the sea, and the waves thereof roar,* Psalm 93:3. Howbeit, because the word, used both here, and there, has oft in it a notion of *quietness,* and *rest,* (see on verse 4.) of *troubling,* or *disturbing,* that I can find, nowhere; I suppose the words may rather, in either place, be rendered, and so also, Jeremiah 31:35, *I the Lord thy God, am he that stilleth the sea,* (that makes it calm and quiet) *when the waves of it roar,* and being able to rule, and still the raging sea, and much more able to curb and quiet the rage of man; and to suppress and quell the power and fury of any oppressor, verse 13, Psalm 75:10, chapter 25:5. This exposition the latter branch much strengthens; nor is there any thing wherein the power of God ordinarily more appears, nor whereby in Scripture it is more frequently extolled, than by the quieting and laying of storms and tempests at sea, and the keeping of that vast and unruly creature within compass, Job 38:8–11, Psalm 65:7 & 77:16,19 & 93:3,4 & 104:6–9 & 107:23–29, Jeremiah 5:22, Jonah 1:4–16, Matthew 8:24,27, Mark 4:39,41, Luke 8:24,25.

*{whose waves roared*} Or, *when the waves thereof roar,* Hebrew, *and its waves roar.* So Proverbs 3:24, chapter 44:14. See God's people on this ground strengthening their faith, in assurance of all-sufficient protection from God, amidst all troubles, turmoils, and tumults whatsoever, Psalm 46:1–3 & 65:7 & 93:3,4.

*{the Lord of hosts is his name*} Or, *whose name is the Lord of hosts,* as chapter 47:4 & 48:2, and does not therefore vainly boast of more than he is able to do, having all creatures at command. See chapter 1:9.

**V. 16.** *{And I have put my words in thy mouth*} Or, as some, *I will put,* etc. There is much doubt, and debate, whom these words should be spoken to. Some would have it spoken to the church of God, to Sion, or Jerusalem: but to it he speaks in the feminine gender, verse 12,17, whereas here, in the masculine. Others, therefore, to the people, of whom the church consists, in the last clause of the verse, to Israel, or Jacob; out of whose mouth, God promises that his word should never depart, chapter 59:20,21. Others, and so most of the Jewish, and some also of ours, conceive that God turns his speech to the prophet, whom he had acquainted with his will, and made choice of to deliver it unto his people, and that in such words and terms as he had prescribed him, or dictated to him. See the like, Numbers 22:35 & 23:5,16, Jeremiah 1:9. And others, lastly, to Christ, whom the Father, had fully opened all his mind unto, concerning what was to be done, in behalf of his church, and appointed him to acquaint his people with it, John 3:32,34 & 5:19,20 & 8:26,28. Or, of all the prophets in general, Christ himself not excluded, by whom, God, through his gracious promises, comforts his church, chapter 40:1, verse 12, Luke 24:25. I concur with those who take the whole passage, as spoken to Esay in particular, thereby to assure his people of the undoubted performance of the things foretold by him, as coming from God himself, who was able to effect them. Yet so, as that they have a further respect to Christ, who, in an higher, and more eminent manner, they also concern. See chapter 49:2 & 61:1,2.

*{and have covered thee under the shadow of mine hand?*} Or, *with the shadow of mine hand have I covered thee.* See chapter 49:2.

*{that I may plant the heavens, and lay the foundations of the earth.*} Hebrew, *to plant an heaven, and to found an earth:* To make a new world, a new heaven, and a new earth, chapter 65:17 & 66:22, 2 Corinthians 5:17,18, 2 Peter 3:13, Revelation 21:1, that which may not amiss be here understood, as said to be done, by Esay ministerially, or prophetically; as the like is said of Jeremy, by preaching, publishing, prophesying, and giving assurance of the doing of it. See Jeremiah 1:10 & 18:9, and the next clause here, by Christ Jesus actually, and effectually, as being the person, by whom the church is planted and built, Jeremiah 31:28, Matthew 16:18, all things in it are made new, Revelation 21:5, and all things both in heaven and earth are restored and settled, Ephesians 1:10, Colossians 1:20. Some, with the ancient Greek, render it, *wherewith* (referring it to the word, *hand,* before mentioned) *I planted the heaven* (or, *stretched it out,* by change of a letter, as verse 13.) *and founded the earth,* as if he had said; I will protect you with the same hand, wherewith heaven and earth were built: and some, *so long as the heavens shall continue built, and the earth founded:* as containing a promise of an everlasting protection. See on verse 6,8. But I see not how the words of the text, though never so much tortured, will yield either of these two.

*{and to say to Zion, Thou art my people*} Or, *Thou shalt again be my people.* See Hosea 1:10 and 2:1,23. Esay, by foretelling; Christ, by fulfilling the restitution of the church, Romans 9:24,26.

**V. 17.** *{Awake, awake*} Or, *Arise, arise.* Hebrew, *Raise,* or *rouse up thyself;* as chapter 64:6. The prophet, or God, by the prophet calling upon the people, as some, to awake and rouse up themselves from the sleep of sin, and the drowsiness of security, 1 Corinthians 15:34, because the apostle seems so to apply it, Ephesians 5:14, though I suppose another place there alluded to. Or, as others, rather, in the first place, at least, and in the literal sense, to raise and rouse up themselves, from that drooping and disconsolate estate and condition, wherein they had long continued, being much dejected and disheartened, during the time of their captivity. See chapter 26:19 & 52:1, implying, that there should be out of hand, a strange and sudden alteration of that their condition.

*{stand up*} Sit no longer on the ground, nor lie in the dust, as the manner of prisoners, and mourners, is wont to be, 2 Samuel 13:16,17, Ezra 9:3, chapter 47:1. See chapter 52:1.

*{O Jerusalem*} The same with Sion, verse 16, the state and people of the Jews, chapter 1:27.

*{that hast drunk at the hand of the Lord, the cup of his fury*} That have sustained grievous things, inflicted on you, by God, for your sins; yea, that began of this cup to others, and have drunk deep of it, Jeremiah 25:15,17,18,29 and 49:12, Ezekiel 23:31.

*{drunk*} Afflictions, in Scripture, are commonly compared to some bitter, unpleasant, yea, or poisonous potion, Jeremiah 8:14 and 9:15 and 23:15, especially considered, as proceeding from God's wrath, Job 21:20.

*{at God's hand*} Hebrew, *from God's hand;* as chapter 50:11, because inflicted on her, by his disposition; in whose hand it is to dispose good and evil, at his pleasure, Psalm 75:6–8, chapter 45:7, Jeremiah 51:7, Lamentations 3:37,38, Habakkuk 2:16.

*{the cup of his fury*} Or, *his cup of wrath,* as the word is well rendered, Deuteronomy 29:28, Job 19:19, Esther 3:5, Psalm 37:8, Proverbs 15:1. For it signifies properly and primarily, *heat.* See chapter 42:25, then *anger,* or, *wrath,* as we also use the word *heat,* when we say, *the man is in a heat:* because anger, causing the blood to boil about the heart, heats, and inflames; *while his heart is hot,* Deuteronomy 19:6, whence also the Latin, *excandescentia.* See chapter 5:25, and yet further, because poison heats, and inflames, the same word is used also for *poison,* Deuteronomy 32:24,33, Psalm 140:4, applied to the Lord's *arrows,* Job 6:4, as here, to his *cup,* and to the wine, in his cup, Jeremiah 25:5, and I see not what should inhibit the rendering of it so here, *his cup of poison,* that is, *his cup tempered with poison:* it has at least sure, some allusion thereunto. See Jeremiah 8:14 & 9:15, Lamentations 3:15. See also, Revelation 14:10 and 16:19.

*{cup*} The word taken from some certain proportion, or allowance of drink, to servants, or other, at meals; or to mariners, and passengers, sometime at sea, is in Scripture used, sometime, for such a portion of favors and mercies, as God is pleased to afford any. So Psalm 16:5. Sometime, for such a quantity of evils, and judgments, as, in his justice, he deems fit to inflict upon any, Psalm 11:6, Lamentations 4:21, Ezekiel 23:31, Matthew 20:22,23 & 26:39, John 18:11, Revelation 18:6.

*{thou hast drunk the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out*} Or, *that hast drunk,* (a defect of the relative, as verse 12.) *and sucking out,* or *in drinking sucked out* (as Psalm 75:8, *the dregs thereof shall they suck out, drink;* that is, *in drinking suck out:* for there is no copulative in either place) *the dregs,* or *lees,* (the word in this passage only used, signifies such thick stuff, as sticks usually to the bottom and comes not so easily away) *of the cup of trembling,* or of *concussion,* or *horror:* as the word it comes of, is well rendered, Nahum 2:3, *the fir trees shall be terribly shaken:* a potion so strangely strong, as makes all that drink it, to stagger, and quake, and shake, in terrible manner, every limb and joint of them. See an instance of it in Baltasar, Daniel 5:6, yea, in Habakkuk himself, Habakkuk 3:16, at the sight only of the character, that forewarned it, with the one; at the bare report of it, with the other. So Psalm 60:2,3, such a potion as made the whole land to shake, as made a terrible earthquake in the whole state; (see chapter 2:19, and so Zechariah 12:2, where some also render it *poison,* as others, *astonishment,* in the psalm; for they that render it *slumbering,* as if it imported some soporiferous potion, seem to warp from the word's original: such a cup they had before drunk, when they were possessed with a spirit of *slumber,* and security, chapter 29:9,10, which was a means to bring on this, that not only roused them out of that security, but cast them into a clean contrary fit, and plight of terror and astonishment, and of this latter, it is here intimated, that she had drunk very deep, when she is said to have drunk it down to the very dregs, yea, to have drained, or *sucked out* the very lowest of it, the lees after the rest, that are usually the strongest, and are reserved for the worst of wicked ones, Psalm 76:8, as the Jewish state is said to have done, both here, and Ezekiel 23:34.

**V. 18.** *{There is none to guide her among all her sons, whom she hath brought forth; neither is there any that taketh her by the hand, of all her sons, that she hath brought up*} Either *that guideth her,* in the former branch; or, *to take her by the hand,* in the latter branch: for the form is the same, to wit, a participle, as also, *of,* or, *from, all her sons,* in either. She had not any one of all those, that had been bred, and brought up in her, neither king, prince, nor prophet that was able to sustain, and hold her up or direct her what course to take, when that dreadful concussion, from that direful potion, before mentioned, verse 17, befell her. See chapter 3:6–8. An allusion to one, that being overmastered with some strong heady drink, has none to lead him or to lend him an hand, to keep him from falling down to the ground, Jeremiah 32:12,14.

*{none to guide her*} Hebrew, *none leading,* or *no leader to her.*

*{brought up*} Or, *reared.* Hebrew, *made great,* as chapter 1:2.

**V. 19.** *{These two things are come unto thee*} Hebrew, *are happened to thee:* for the Holy Ghost does not waive that term. See Ecclesiastes 8:14 & 9:11, nor our Savior himself, Luke 10:31, and it is used of those things, that fall out beyond man's expectation, and foresight without his contrivement, or beside his intent and purpose. See the like, chapter 47:9.

*{Who shall be sorry for thee?*} Or, as some, *Who is sorry for thee?* as if it were said, and yet who takes your afflictions to heart? or is at all affected with them, as implying, that she had been utterly abandoned in them, Jeremiah 15:5, Lamentations 1:12 & 2:15. Or, *who shall mourn,* (as it is expressed, Job 2:11.) or, *lament* (as Psalm 69:20.) *with thee.* Or, *who shall bemoan thee?* as it is rendered, Jeremiah 15:5, Nahum 3:7, for it has not a bare notion of *sorrow,* or *grief:* but such an expression of a fellow feeling of the miseries of another, whereby the same is made known unto him, and that for this end, to help, if it may be, in some degree, to lighten, and lessen his heaviness and grief: and these two, are ordinarily yoked together, *condoling,* and *comforting,* both in some of the places before mentioned, Job 2:11, Psalm 69:20, Jeremiah 15:5, and in this.

*{desolation, and destruction, and the famine, and the sword*} Hebrew, *devastation,* and *contrition,* or *breaking,* as we say, *to shivers:* for from hence our *shiver* seems to come. So chapter 1:28 & 30:13,14. He spoke of two, he reckons up four; the question is, how this seeming difference may be reconciled? Some, by the two, at first propounded, understand those two before related, *desolation,* or *affliction,* from the wrath of God, by the enemy, from abroad, called also, *God's cup,* Jeremiah 51:7, verse 17, and want of consolation, of means to relieve and support her, from any of her own, at home; none of them affording her, or being able to tender unto her, the *cup of consolation,* Jeremiah 16:7, verse 18, both also here intimated: in the numeration of evils, the one; in the questions concerning the condoling with her, and comforting of her, the other. See chapter 54:11. Others suppose that those two evils, are contained in these four terms; the evils comprised in them, though branched into four sprigs, yet reducible to two heads, to wit, either, evils during the siege of the city, *hunger,* and *sword,* and evils, ensuing the surprisal of it, *devastation,* and *destruction,* or, evils concerning the city, *devastation,* and *destruction,* and evils concerning the citizens, *famine* and *sword:* or, as some others, supposing them to be twice repeated, *desolation,* and *destruction:* and again, as the same, in effect, with the former, *famine,* and *the sword,* that is, as if he had said, *desolation by famine,* and *destruction by the sword:* but these latter seem more coact: the first to have least force; the rather for that these four here mentioned, were all ingredients of that cup of wrath, that poisonful potion, that God in his just judgment, had deservedly reached out to them.

*{by whom should I comfort thee?*} Or, *whom shall I make to comfort thee?* as some: but that without example; rather as our version, *By whom:* a defect of the particle, as chapter 63:12. By whose help, or aid, should relief be procured for you? as Nahum 3:7. Or, by what example of others, that have been in like distress, should I assay to minister comfort to you, as implying, that her calamity was matchless, without example, or precedent. So Lamentations 2:13. The former suits better with that before, verse 18, and that after, verse 20. The preposition is wanting; as Psalm 17:14. Now all this is here inserted, to show, that notwithstanding this her forlorn, and desperate condition, God was able to raise, and restore her, and would do it.

**V. 20.** *{Thy sons*} Of whom, verse 18.

*{have fainted*} Or, *do faint:* as Jonah 4:8, Amos 8:13, they that should help to relieve, and sustain you, verse 18, or, to condole with you, and comfort you, verse 19, are in as bad plight, as yourself, Lamentations 1:11,12 & 2:11,12.

*{they lie*} *they faint, they lie;* that is, they lie fainting: as, *they hasted, they forgat,* for, *they soon forgat,* Psalm 116:13.

*{in the head of all the streets*} That is, in the city of Jerusalem, at the end, beginning, or entrance of every street there, where they either had been surprised, and seized on, by the enemy, like beasts, taken in a toil, Lamentations 4:18–20, Ezekiel 19:4,8, or, lay starved, and pining with famine, for want of food, Lamentations 2:19 and 4:5. *head of the streets,* Nahum 3:10, as, *head of the ways,* Ezekiel 16:25,31.

*{as a wild bull in a net*} As that fierce creature, when he is taken in the huntsman's toil, and so mashed, and entangled in it, that he is by no means able to wind himself out, though having clean spent himself, by striving so to do: what creature it should be, that is here mentioned, the Jewish doctors themselves are very uncertain. Some of them tell us, it is a kind of bird, or fowl; but of what kind they say not: and that is apparently false; for it is mentioned among the beasts allowed for food, Deuteronomy 14:5, and it is therefore most generally agreed on, to be a beast; which some of the Jewish masters affirm to be a kind of *wild ox,* or *bull;* which our version follows, nor do those seem to have swerved from the same notion, that render it, *Bubalis,* a *buffal,* or a *bugel:* for howsoever the word *Bubalus,* is, with the ancient Greeks and Latins, the name of a beast in Africk, not much bigger than a calf, and shaped somewhat like a stag; whereof, see Oppian l. 2. Yet Pliny tells us, l. 8, c. 15, that even in his time, the common sort of people had begun to give that name to the *Uri,* a kind of wild oxen, that Germany bred; whereof Cesar, in his sixth book of his *war with the Galles,* tells; that some were not much less than an elephant. See on chapter 34:7. The ancient Greek version, and old Latin translation in Moses, render it *Oryx.* This Aristotle, in his *history of living creatures,* l. 2, c. 1, says, is single horned, and cloven footed: and so Pliny, in his *natural story,* l. 11, c. 46, who further, l. 8, c. 53 affirms it, to be a kind of *wild goat,* whose hair grows toward his head: But Oppian, in his *hunting treatises,* l. 2, describes it, as a very fierce beast; not much less than the *rhinoceros* (for height I suppose he means, rather, than for bulk of body) with upright, massy, exceeding hard, and sharp horns, wherewith he would venture upon any beast, wild boar, wild bull, leopard, or lion: and this author may the better be herein credited; because in his times, this beast came to be exhibited, in public shows, at Rome, where Martial tells us, it cost the price of many a dog, l. 13, Epigr. 95, for those things that Ælian, and Orus relate of it, seem fabulous.
