Now on the other side, those people that were their adversaries and oppressors, shall be made to endure much calamity, and sustain a great deal of misery, while God's people shall enjoy peace and plenty, chap. 13.1,2. & 65.13,14.

*{darkness*} For, *adversity*; as chap. 59.9. spiritual darkness, where the light of God's word, and Spirit, is wanting, chap. 8.20. & 9.2. & 59.21. Luke 1.79. Acts 26.18.

*{thick darkness*} The word seems compounded of a term, that signifies *to drop*, or *distill*; as Deut. 32.2. & 33.28. and another that signifies *a mist*, or *fog*; chap. 29.18. & 59.9. so that it implies in its proper notion, a mist, so thick, that it even drops again: such a mist, or darkness, as that in Egypt was, Exod. 10.22,23.

*{But the Lord shall arise upon thee.*} The Messiah, the Sun of righteousness shall arise, and shine forth upon you, with healing in his wings, Mal. 4.2. an allusion to the light, that in Goshen they enjoyed, when all Egypt was overspread with palpable darkness, Exod. 10.23.

*{and his glory shall be seen upon thee.*} As it was sometime upon the sanctuary, Lev. 9.23,24. See vers. 1.

**V. 3.** *{And Gentiles shall come to thy light, and Kings to the brightness of thy rising.}* Or, *Nations shall walk in*, or, *by thy light, and Kings, by the brightness of thy rising*, as John 12.35. Rev. 21.24. not, shall repair together only, to congratulate with you, as Chap. 39.1. & 66.10. but to adjoin themselves unto you, and to enjoy light together with you, Chap. 56.6,7. & 62.2. & 66.11.

*{the brightness of thy rising.*} Your resplendent luster, partly, in temporal dignity, but principally in spiritual excellency, upon this your restitution, Chap. 62.3. the church being as the morning star, shining bright, with light received from Christ, Rev. 2.28. & 12.1. the fountain of all true light, John 1.4,9. Or, as some render it, *the brightness that riseth upon thee*, vers. 1,2.

**V. 4.** *{Lift up thine eyes round about thee, and see:*} See Chap. 49.18.

*{all they, gather themselves together, they come to thee.*} Or, *and come to thee*; as some here render it; and as it was before rendered, Chap. 49.18. or, *those all* (as if in a vision, he showed them a numberless number of people, flocking together from all parts) *are gathered together to come unto thee*; as Zeph. 3.7. *they rose up early, they corrupted their doings*, for, *they rose early to corrupt* them. Or, *all those that gather themselves together* (this great multitude that you see gathered together, a defect of the relative; as Chap. 58.5.) *do all come*, or, *are all coming to thee*, Chap. 49.18. & 54.2,3.

*{thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed by thy side.*} That is, as some, your children shall all be brought home to you; some from places more remote; some from places nearer at hand, where they were nursed beside you, or at your side: as others, your sons shall be brought from far, and your daughters shall, as nurse-children, *be carried at the side*, that is, in the arms, on the one side of those, who as nurses shall bring them: and this by collation of the place, with Chap. 49.22. and 66.13. seems to be the genuine sense of the place. For, as for that nicety of some, that the males, as the stronger, are said to *come*; the females, as the weaker, *to be brought in arms*; it seems overcurious, as may appear by comparing this with Chap. 49.22. where the *sons* are said to be brought in *laps*, or *bosoms*, and the *daughters* borne on *shoulders*. It is but a rhetorical amplification, illustrate by a *distribution*, the terms whereof, may be indifferently, and interchangeably applied unto either subject. Whereof see more on chap. 5.13. If we follow our version, there is a defect of the pronoun; as chap. 38.13. Howbeit some supply another way, reading it, *at their side*, or *beside them*, as Job 1.14. (though another word be there used) that is, beside your sons, coming jointly along with them: a sense not improbable; but I adhere rather to the first.

**V. 5.** *{Then shalt thou see and flow together:*} Or, as some, *flow over*: break out, as a river that surrounds its banks, chap. 54.1. But rather retaining our received version; when this shall befall you, you shall sit feeding your eyes, as it were with the pleasing sight of it: and the heart shall even wave, and flow, in a manner, to and fro, through abundance of joy within you, at the view of that great multitude, that you shall see come flocking into you, and flowing in upon you: for that is the proper, and general signification of the word here used: Which yet some render *thou shalt shine*; because from it is derived a word rendered *light*, Job 3.4. & Dan. 2.22. and thence gather, that the verb itself signifies *to shine*, both here (as if it were said, *thou shalt shine* out gloriously in your full luster; as Job 29.3.) and elsewhere, Psal. 34.5. But the word of *light* seems to have its original from this root; as it has a notion of *confluence*, or *influence*, in it. Nor is there any necessity, that it should signify *to shine*, either in the one place, or in the other.

*{and thine heart shall fear,*} Not through dread, or terror, but with admiration, and joys sudden and excessive, cause a trembling, or fluttering of the heart many times, together with the dilatation of it, Gen. 45.26,27. Jer. 33.9. Hos. 3.5. Acts 2.7. & 12.14. and this more fully explains what was before said *thou shalt flow* upon the sight of it.

*{and be enlarged:*} For joy dilates & enlarges the heart, 2 Cor. 6.11,12. as on the contrary grief is wont to contract and draw it in, Prov. 12.25. See chap. 61.3.

*{because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come into thee.*} Or, *when the abundance*, or, *multitude*, (for, *noise*, which some would fetch in from chap. 17.12. and 63.15. fits not here) *of the sea* (of the sea itself: Of which, see on vers. 6. Or, of those that coast on the sea, or trade by sea; as chap. 23.2,4.) *shall be turned into thee*, or, *toward thee*, (as 2 King. 5.26.) or, *upon thee* (as 1 Sam. 4.19. Dan. 10.16. because there follows, vers. 6. *shall cover thee*. Nor need we, as some of note do, to make it a complexive form, like that, 1 Sam. 7.2. as if the meaning at full expressed were, *shall be converted, and come into thee*) *and the wealth* (as the word is used, Job 20.15. Prov. 13.22. Chap. 8.8. & 61.6.) Or, *the troops*, (because the verb is plural both here and vers. 11.) *of the nations, shall come to thee*. The meaning is, that people out of all parts shall repair to God's church, and betaking themselves thereunto, honor him, and it, to their utmost ability, by tendering both themselves, and whatsoever they are stored with, unto his service, and to the service of his church, chap. 23.18. & 49.23. & 61.6. 2 Cor. 8.3–5. For they draw it too low, that fetch in hither, the markets kept at Jerusalem, and the fish, and other wares, brought in thither, by the merchants of Tyre, Neh. 13.16.

**V. 6.** *{The multitude of camels shall cover thee;*} The word rendered *multitude*, does signify, in the first place, a great *affluence*, or *abundance* of aught. Hence, Deut. 33.19. *the abundance of the sea*; that is, of such commodities as the seas afford; (and so also might that in the foregoing verse be understood; but that the word there used, does rather signify, *a multitude of people*, chap. 13.4.) and *abundance of waters*, Job 22.11. But sometime it is used for some great *troop*, or *company*, of men, 2 King. 9.17. or horse, Ezek. 26.10. here, of camels, which were much used for carriage of wares, and commodities, in those parts, ch. 21.7. & 30.6. said, for the multitude of them, *to cover* the country; as those of the Midianites, Judg. 6.5. So, *abundance of waters*, *to cover*, Job 22.11. and those companies of horse, *to cover with dust*, Ezek. 26.10. Yet we need not therefore with the Latin, render it, *an inundation*; because of *waters*, the word is used, and they are said *to cover the earth*, Jer. 46.8. and much less, as some would have it, that the camels should be said to cover the land, with the dust that they should raise with their feet.

*{the dromedaries,*} The Greek renders it as the former, *Camels*: And our Jewish critics would make us believe, that the young camels are thus called, so long as they suck; and that when they are once weaned, then they begin to be called, *Camels*; because the verb of which root it seems to be, signifies sometime *to nurse*, and *to wean*, Gen. 1.8. 1 Sam. 1.22–24. as if nursing, and weaning, were the camels' peculiar, and not common to them, with other creatures. They might as well affirm, that camels are so called; for that they use to nurse their old dams, and sires, as they say of the *stork*; (as truly, it may be, as of the *swan's singing* towards her end) because the word signifies, as commonly, *to retribute*, & *repay*, Deut. 32.6. 1 Sam. 24.18. 2 Sam. 22.21. it is well known that in Hebrew, as well as in other languages, from the same root, for letters and sound, divers words spring: that in use and notion have no affinity at all one with another. Of which, see on Jer. 24.2. but that this is a frivolous figment of theirs, is apparent: For it is absurd to imagine, that the people here mentioned should bring no camels, but *weanlings*, or *unweaned ones*, rather, or should bring their wares and commodities on the backs of such: the feminine word is used, Jer. 2.23,24. of a beast running at large, and joined with the wild ass, that runs a madding in genituring times after the male. The term is nowhere found, save in the masculine, here; in the feminine there. It seems to be, as the old Latin renders it, that which the Greeks, and the Latin, from them, as we, from the Latins, term *a dromedary*, or *a dromas*; a beast commended for swiftness, Jer. 2.23. whence also it has its name in Greek, and, as some would have it also, but that is somewhat too far-fetched in Hebrew: For, because from the same root arises, both the word, that signifies, *firstborn*, and *firstfruits*; and that, whereby this beast is named, therefore they deem it so called; because, in pace, it outgoes other beasts, as the firstborn comes before other issue. But that seems true also here, that was hinted before, concerning diversity of notions, meeting in one root. The *dromas* is a lesser and lower kind of camel, very rife in Arabia, though used much for burden, yet of special commendation for swiftness, and by couriers therefore generally, in those parts employed. See of them, Strabo, lib. 15. Diodor. lib. 2. c. 54. Livy, lib. 37. Leo the Africane, li. 9.

*{of Midian*} People descended from Abraham by Keturah, Gen. 25.2. that had their seat in Arabia, mixed with the Ismaelites, as appears, Gen. 37.25,28. and with the Cushites; as appears, Num. 12.1. Hab. 3.7.

*{and Ephah,*} The posterity of Midian, by his eldest son, Gen. 25.4.

*{all they from Sheba shall come*} The posterity of Chush, by his fourth son Raamah, Gen. 10.7. Psal. 72.10.

*{they shall bring gold, and incense.*} The chief commodities of their country, 1 King. 10.2,10. chap. 61.6. Ezek. 27.22. Mat. 2.11.

*{and they shall show forth the praises of the Lord.*} Repairing thither, not for traffic, but to worship, Acts 8.27.

**V. 7.** *{All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together unto thee:*} Or, *shall be gathered together, and come*: or, *be brought to thee*; as it is more fully, vers. 4. Or, *shall be gathered together to bring to thee*. See the like form of speech, Gen. 27.9. Chap. 38.21. The *Kedarens*, or, *Arabians*, called by the Greeks, *Scenitæ* of the *tents* they lived in. See chap. 21.16. they abounded in cattle, Ezek. 27.21.

*{The rams of Nebaioth shall minister unto thee:*} The issue of Nebaioth, Ismael’s firstborn, elder brother to Kedar, Gen. 25.13. called in later times by the Greeks and Latins, *Nabateans*, whom Strabo, l. 16. places in Arabia; as also, Pliny, l. 5. c. 11. where he joins them, and the *Cedreans*, together.

*{they shall come up with acceptance upon mine altar:*} Being made burnt offerings, thence so termed, Chap. 1.11. See chap. 56.7. Psal. 51.19.

*{and I will glorify the house of my glory.*} Or, *for* (as chap. 59.17.) *I will adorn*, or *make magnificent, my beautiful*, or, *magnificent*, or *goodly house*: *a house of beauty, magnificence*, or, *goodliness*; as, a *crown* of the like, chap. 62.3. and, a *name* of the like, chap. 63.14. his temple he means; a type of his church, chap. 2.2. See vers. 13.

**V. 8.** *{What are these that fly as a cloud; and as the doves to their windows?*} As before, vers. 4. So here again, the prophet speaks, as if in a vision he saw multitudes of people, by shoals, making towards Jerusalem, like clouds, that come oft from remote parts, driven, swiftly, by the wind, chap. 19.1. Jer. 4.13. and coming so thick, that they cover the whole face of the heaven, and intercept the skylight, Psal. 147.8. Ezek. 38.9. Joel 2.2. Heb. 12.1. Or, like doves, or pigeons, that fly in great flocks, & that with much speed, to their places of retreat and refuge, either when they perceive a storm towards, or when by fowls of prey they are pursued, Psal. 11.1. as Noahs did, when she could find no rest elsewhere, to the ark, Gen. 8.9. There is in it an intimation, as of those multitudes of people, that should come into the church, and adjoin themselves thereunto, Acts 2.37,40,41. & 4.4. Heb. 12.1,22,23. So of the speed and eagerness that they should express, in their repair thither, Jer. 50.8. Matth. 11.12. Luke 12.1. Some interpreters of note, read the words, not, *who*, but *whose are these*; making it the speech of Sion, or the church; not unlike that, chap. 49.21. *who begat these?* Which some the rather embrace, because the interrogative seems to be of a singular notion only. But it is found joined with the very same term, in a plural notion also, Gen. 33.5. *Who are these?* and may well therefore stand as our version has it. Nor does it hinder, but that it may be fitly deemed, though so read, a question moved by Sion, whom the prophet had called upon, as in a vision to see people flocking towards her, vers. 4.

*{and as the doves*} Or, *or as the doves*: for they are two divers resemblances. So chap. 1.30. & 6.13.

*{that fly*} A defect of the relative; as chap. 58.5.

*{doves to their windows*} Or, *louvers*, or *lockers*: to the loopholes of the turrets in which they keep: a fit resemblance of the Jews returning from Babylon to their former places of abode: as doves at time of year, in some parts, to their wonted nests.

**V. 9.** *{Surely the isles shall wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, to bring thy sons from far*} This seems an answer returned, as in God's person, by the prophet, to Sions question. As if he should say, Do you ask who they are? They are your children whom the sea-coasters, and islanders have, by mine appointment, with their ships, been attending on, to bring them home to you.

*{Surely*} So is this particle used, chap. 7.9,16. & 49.18. Some render it here, *For*.

*{The isles*} Such as dwell on the seacoast, or deal in shipping, as chap. 41.4. & 51.5. & 59.18. See vers. 5.

*{shall wait for me*} Or, *have waited on me*; as chap. 8.17. & 30.18. attending when to be employed by me.

*{and the ships of Tarshish*} As being fittest, and readiest at hand, for transportation of persons into those parts. See chap. 2.16. & 23.1.

*{first*} That is, as some, *with the first*; or, among the first of them, that have an hand in bringing of God's people home. Others, *at the first*; as implying, that the first of these, that returned, should be brought home, with most ease, as if they had come by shipping. Others, carrying it back to the first words, *shall wait on me in the first place*; and on you, and yours, in the next, 2 Cor. 8.5. Others, *with a principal one*, to wit, ship; to be as admiral to the fleet: Or lastly, as others, (inserting the note of similitude, frequently suppressed: as Psal. 11.1.) *as formerly*, or, *as at first*; as chap. 1.26. and they suppose it to have an eye back to Solomons days: wherein ships of Tarshish brought Solomon store of treasure, 1 King. 9.26–28. & 10.12. this may seem the more probable, because mention of such matter follows. Yet I go rather (because it goes more smoothly off) with the first.

*{to bring thy sons*} Your children home from the places of their captivity; as chap. 49.22. & 66.20. vers. 4. implying, that they should get home as easily, as if they were borne in arms, or carried in litters, or conveyed by shipping. See Gal. 4.26.

*{from afar*} As vers. 4. no distance of place being able to hinder the return of any of God's captived ones, into their own country; nor remoteness of place, or state, the access of any unto God, by Christ, chap. 43.6. Jer. 30.10. Eph. 2.13.

*{their silver, and their gold, with them,*} Either that which themselves bring as a freewill offering for God's service, and the beautifying of his temple, ver. 6. or, the treasure that God's people shall bring along with them, for more ease, and safety, together with their persons, conveying it for them, as pointing unto that gold and silver, that strangers should furnish them with, at their return, for their journey, and the vessels that were to be sent back again with them, Ezra 1.4,6–11.

*{unto the name of the Lord thy God, and to the Holy One of Israel*} That is, unto the place that the Lord has chosen, to place his name there, Deut. 12.5. the temple, a type of the church, there to present them as an offering to God, chap. 66.20. Rom. 15.16. or, *for the name of the Lord thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel*; out of that reverent, and religious respect and regard that they shall have unto the Lord your God, Ezr. 1.2,3. & 6.8–12. See chap. 55.5. Of the titles given God here, see chap. 1.4. & 41.13,14.

*{because he hath glorified thee*} Or, as some, *when he shall have glorified thee*: as by temporal deliverance; so by the ministry of the gospel settled with you, chap. 55.5. See chap. 2.2. Zach. 8.23. or, *for he will make thee goodly*, or *magnificent*; he is resolved to make you stately. See vers. 7. the same word is in either place.

**Vers. 10.** *{And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls;*} That is, *strangers* themselves; being now become proselytes, chap. 56.6. & 61.5. shall join with you, in furthering the restoration of the city; and shall help to carry on the gracious work of spiritual edification, 1 Thess. 5.11.

*{and their Kings shall minister unto thee:*} Cyrus, and other his successors, that shall supply you with necessaries, and accommodations in divers kind, Ezra 1.4,8. & 7.12–26. Neh. 2.8. but those especially by the ministry of the gospel, won to the profession of the Christian faith, chap. 49.7,23. & 52.15. v. 3.

*{for in my wrath I smote thee,*} Chap. 57.17. Jer. 30.14. Lam. 3.1.

*{but in my favor have I had mercy on thee*} Chap. 12.1. & 14.1. & 54.8.

*{but*} Or, *yet*: though in wrath I smote you, yet out of my free favor I will now restore you. chap. 57.18. Lam. 3.32. Heb. *and*: as chap. 12.1.

**V. 11.** *{Therefore shall thy gates be open continually, they shall not be shut day nor night*} Heb. *They shall open thy gates*: as chap. 26.3. or, *thy gates shall open themselves*: as chap. 48.8. Acts 12.10. they shall be opened, that is, stand open: as *wasted*, for, lie waste, chap. 34.10. *builded*, for, stand built, Dan. 9.25. they shall stand open night and day, in regard of continual concourse, and confluence of people: and as in times of general peace and security, is wont to be, when all is quiet on every side, as some in Christ's time suppose it to have been at Jerusalem; from Luke 21.37. & John 18.1. but of that some doubt may be; though at that time, in regard of the Paschal solemnity whereto out of all parts they resorted, it might for some short space so be. See Rev. 21.25.

*{that men may bring to thee the forces of the Gentiles*} Or, *the wealth*. See vers. 5. Heb. *to bring the forces*, or, *wealth of the nations*; that is, *that the forces of the nations* (subdued in fight) or, *their wealth* (and spoils taken in fight) *may be brought into thee*; as some: or, simply, for the bringing in of them in any kind, or any way whatsoever, vers. 5,6,7.

*{and that their Kings may be brought*} Heb. *and their Kings led*: Which word, because it is sometime used of *leading captive*; as chap. 20.4. the Chaldee (whom divers others also therein follow) does so here understand: according to that, Psal. 149.8. Chap. 45.14. Howbeit, others, both Jewish and ours, understand it of kings *led*, that is, conducted in state; as they use to go ushered with officers going before them, to clear the way for them: so is the word used, 2 King. 4.24. and it may very well be so taken in this place, of kings entering with their attendants, conducting them in state: and the whole passage may be read, *for the bringing in of the wealth of the nations, and of their Kings led in state*. So, rather, than as one of good note, *the wealth of their nations, and of their Kings, which* (wealth, or riches, because the participle is plural) *shall be borne before them*: as 1 Sam. 30.20. Chap. 8.4. for this syntax seems overharsh; the meaning is, that not the people alone, but their rulers also, should render themselves and their means serviceable unto God's church.

**V. 12.** *{For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee, shall perish*} All people, or persons, great, or small, that shall refuse to submit to the scepter and government of Christ erected in you, Psal. 110.2. to be swayed by his word, and Spirit, chap. 59.21. shall everlastingly perish, Psal. 2.12. 2 Cor. 2.16. & 4.3. it seems to be an allusion unto the condition of those, that refused to submit unto the people of God, when they entered upon the land of Canaan, Deut. 20.10–17. See Zach. 14.16–19.

*{nation and kingdom*} Or, *nation, or kingdom*: as Exod. 21.15. & 55.29.

*{yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted*} Heb. *and* (as c. 55.1.) *those nations* (to wit, that will not serve you, to be supplied from the former branch, as Gen. 1.16.) *shall by being wasted, be wasted*, or, *being destroyed be destroyed*: See the like, Deut. 7.2. & 20.17.

**V. 13.** *{The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary.*} The goodly cedars, and other choice trees, wherewith Lebanon abounds, affording materials fit for stately buildings, shall be brought in, great store of them, to build and beautify my temple, alluding to the plenty of cedars, and other timber trees, that Solomon procured to be brought from Lebanon, for the building of God's temple, 1 King. 5.10,14,18.

*{glory of Lebanon*} That is, the cedars, which were of prime and chief note among the trees of the forest, Ezek. 31.3,8. and Lebanon of prime note, above other places, for them, Psal. 104.16. chap. 2.13. & 37.24.

*{the fir*} These also of much use for building, chap. 14.8. and Lebanon for them also famous, chap. 37.24.

*{the pine and the box*} See of these on cap. 41.19.

*{to beautify*} Or, *adorn*: as, Ezra 7.27. See vers. 7.

*{and I will make the place of my feet glorious*} Or, *for* (as v. 7. c. 59.17.) *I will make glorious* (I am resolved to bestow abundance of spiritual glory, 2 Cor. 3.7–11,18. upon) *the place of my feet*: so, *the place of the soles of my feet*, Ezek. 43.7. that is, of my special rest, and residence, chap. 11.10. so was, in times past, esteemed, and termed, first the ark, styled his *footstool*, 1 Chr. 28.2. Psal. 99.5. & 132.7. then the temple, and Sion whereon it stood, called his *rest*, Psal. 78.68,69. & 132.13,14. all resembling the church, 1 Tim. 3.15. Rev. 21.3.

**V. 14.** *{The sons also of them, that afflicted thee, shall come bending unto thee, and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down, at the soles of thy feet*} Those that were before your adversaries, shall now come into you, and submit themselves unto you, and to the scepter of the Messiah, erected with you, chap. 49.23. Rev. 3.9. See ver. 12.

*{The sons also of them that afflicted thee*} Heb. *And* (as chap. 57.8,15.) *the sons of thine afflicters*; their *children*: or, they themselves, as, *the sons of strangers*, ver. 10. and so in the next branch, *the despisers of thee*; or both.

*{and they shall call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel*} Either you shall be so called, the verb taken indefinitely, as chap. 62.12. or even they themselves being convinced in conscience of the truth hereof, shall now acknowledge you, whom before they contemned, and maligned, oppugned and oppressed, to be the Lord's own royal city, and the place of his Holiness's special residence, Ezek. 48.53. See their acknowledgment, ch. 49.23.

**V. 15.** *{Whereas thou hast been forsaken, and hated, so that no man went through thee*} During the time of your depopulation, while your people were abroad in captivity, ch. 3.26. & 6.11,12. Jer. 9.11,12.

*{hated*} Disregarded, disesteemed; as Deut. 21.15. Mat. 6.24. not sought to, or looked after, Jer. 30.17.

*{so that no man went through thee*} Heb. *and no passenger*; or, *and without passenger*; as chap. 24.10. Jer. 9.9. a defect of the pronoun: as chap. 5.23. & 58.9.

*{I will make thee an eternal excellency*} Heb. *an excellency of eternity*, or, *perpetuity*; as chap. 63.12. a lasting excellency.

*{a joy of many generations*} Heb. *of generation, and generation*; as chap. 24.17.

**V. 16.** *{Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles, and shalt suck the breast of Kings:*} *also*. Heb. *and*, as ver. 14. All, as well high, as low, shall with their endowments, and abilities, of what kind soever, supply you, succor you, support you, nourish you, being as foster fathers, or nurses, to you, as Mordecai was to Ester, Est. 2.7. ver. 4. chap. 49.26. & 66.12.

*{the breast of Kings*} So is the word rendered, and seems to be used, Job 24.9. Howbeit, the word that signifies *a teat*, or *dug*, is somewhat divers from this. See chap. 28.9. & 32.12. Lam. 4.3. and some therefore interpret it, not the *breast*, or *teat* itself; but the moisture drawn from it: and there want not of the Jewish critics, who understand by the phrase here, such *dainties*, as kings are wont to be fed with.

*{and thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Savior, and thy Redeemer, the mighty one of Jacob*} Or, *that thou mayst know*, (by good proof, and experience, find it so to be; as Ezek. 34.30. either implying the issue of it: as Ezek. 30.25. or, the end of doing it, as chap. 45.3.) *that I the Lord am thy Savior, and that the mighty one of Jacob is thy Redeemer*. See chap. 49.26.

**V. 17.** *{For brass I will bring gold; and for iron, I will bring silver; and for wood, brass, and for stones, iron:*} I will make reparations of all your losses, and damages, with advantage; all things shall be exceedingly improved, and changed with you, for the better, ch. 30.26. & 35.13. an allusion to the wealth of the Jewish state in Solomons days. Of which, see King. 10.27. 2 Chr. 1.15. & 9.27.

*{I will also make thine officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness*} *also*. Heb. *and*: as ver. 16. Because there can be no assured continuance, or constant enjoyment of wealth, and plenty in a state unsettled, and wherein peace and equity are not established; God therefore promises to furnish their state with such rulers, and officers, as should be careful to demean themselves equally, and uprightly in their places, and to maintain the people, subject unto them, in prosperity and peace.

*{thine officers peace*} Or, *thine officers officers of peace*, or, *men of peace*: as Psal. 120.7. *I am peace*: that is, *a man of peace*: one that affect, desire, seek, study peace; but here rather *officers of peace*: with supply from the other term: as chap. 10.1. Dan. 4.33. they shall be such, as shall seek and study your prosperity and welfare, (so is *peace* commonly taken, chap. 48.18. Psal. 122.9.) Neh. 2.10. Ezek. 34.23. Heb. *thine office*, Psal. 109.8. or, *oversight*, as Num. 3.22. or, *government*, for, *officers, overseers* or, *governors*: (for the word it comes of, is used oft for *officers*, with charge of government: as Jer. 20.1.) as *kingdom*, or, *royalty*, for, *Kings*, Jer. 19.7. it may, without any force to the text, be rendered, *I will make thy government a government of peace*, that is, *a peaceable government*; not embroiled in wars, nor taken up with military employments, as in time past.

*{thine exactors righteousness*} Or *overseers*; as the ancient Greek renders it: the old Latin, *those that are set over thee*: the word is usually taken in the worse part, for *exactors, oppressors*, chap. 3.12. & 9.4. & 14.2. yet not always, but sometime, for *rulers, overseers*, or *officers*; such as either take, or gather toll and tribute; or oversee those that are in any employment, or work: so it is taken, Zach. 10.4. and so here; *thy rulers*, or *overseers, righteousness*; or, rulers, overseers, *of righteousness*; that is, just and righteous: not such as shall pill, and poll you, exact upon you, and oppress you as formerly; but such as shall carry themselves moderately, and mercifully: (for so is *righteousness* also used, Psal. 112.3,9.) See chap. 1.23,26. & 32.1,2. Neh. 5.15. Ezek. 23.4,16.

**V. 18.** *{Violence shall no more be heard in thy land; wasting nor destruction within thy borders*} You shall live quietly and peaceably, free from oppression, by bad rulers within you: and free from invasion, and incursion, by hostility from abroad, Psal. 10.16. and 144.24,25. chap. 16.4. Ezek. 34.26–28. Zach. 9.8.

*{wasting, and destruction*} Or, *devastation, and destruction*. See chap. 59.7.

*{but thou shalt call thy walls salvation, and thy gates praise.*} That is, they shall be such unto you; for to be called this, or that, is in Scripture language so to be. See chap. 7.14. & 9.6. & 47.1. & 56.7. ver. 14. either your *walls*, and *gates*, shall be *safety*, and *praise*, to you; that is, shall afford you safety, and minister matter to you, of praising God for it: or, *salvation*, and *praise*, shall be *wall*, and *gate*, to you, that is, God's protection, for which you shall have cause daily to praise him, shall be sufficient, instead of walls, and gates, to secure you. See the like expression, chap. 26.2. See also, Psal. 147.12,14. the meaning is, that all should be safe with them, under God's protection: by means whereof, they should have liberty to serve him the more cheerfully, Luk. 1.74,75. Act. 9.31. Nor is that explication of theirs, wholly impertinent, that would have it to be implied, that the watchmen, placed on the walls usually, or over the gates, chap. 62.6. 2 Sam. 18.24. should not be taken up, with solicitous looking out, or expecting of some enemy's approach, but being freed from fear of aught in that kind, should sit securely, passing their time, in singing of praises unto God, chap. 52.8. Howbeit, to draw out to such particulars, is not needful. Nor is that of some others altogether unsuitable, that God would continually come to them with new favors, and they go forth with praises, to meet him, Psal. 89.15–17. But I suppose, that both *wall*, and *gate*, here, are in a notion of defense; and the rather mention seems to be made hereof, to comfort God's people, when they should be, without gate, or wall, for some time after their return; to give them assurance of safety notwithstanding the want of such material fortifications, and defenses. See Neh. 1.3. & 2.13,17. & 4.2,3. Zach. 2.4,5. Nor can I therefore accord with those, who refer *gates* here, to execution of justice: because the gate was commonly, the place of judicature. Lam. 5.14.

**V. 19.** *{The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.*} Matter of safety was before, ver. 18. Matter of joy, and solace, now follows: both joined together, in *sun*, and *shield*, Psal. 84.11. The meaning is not, that after their return from captivity, in their state restored, or at any time in this world, God's people in any place, should have no use of those celestial bodies, to impart light unto them: but that their chief, and principal light and comfort, should consist in such a plentiful enjoyment of God's gracious favor, and lovingkindness, that in comparison thereof, these external lights should be as of no regard, or account. Though there want not those, who refer this wholly unto the glorious estate of God's children in the next life; when all these outward ordinary means of joy and comfort; temporal, or spiritual, expiring, or surceasing, God himself shall immediately become all in all unto his: and then indeed shall be the consummated complement of it, 1 Cor. 15.28. See Rev. 21.23.

*{The Lord an everlasting light*} Heb. *a light of perpetuity*, or, *of eternity*; as, *joy of perpetuity*, or *eternity*, chap. 35.10. a constant light: such a light as has no variation, or shadow of change, with it; as these bodily lights oft have, Jam. 1.17. a light that shines, as well by night, as by day; a light that never sets, but shines to all eternity, ver. 20. Of this light, see Psal. 4.6,7. & 27.1. & 30.5. & 36.9,10. & 43.3. & 84.11. & 89.15.

*{for brightness*} Or, *for luster* by night; as some supply from the opposite member, in the former branch; as the like supply would be from the latter branch, in the former, Psal. 105.39. *he spread a cloud for a covering* by day, *and fire to give light by night*.

**V. 20.** *{Thy sun shall no more go down, neither shall the moon withdraw itself.*} God's grace and free favor, in the comfortable influences, and effects of it, that shall be as sun, and moon, to you, shall be in a plentiful manner, without interruption, continually present with you, Rev. 22.5. it shall not be clouded, or eclipsed towards you, as in former times; by occasion of offense, and displeasure for your sins, chap. 54.8,9. & 59.2. Lam. 4.44. Or, as some, you shall not any more be through straits and distresses, surprised and possessed, with such anxiety, and perplexity, of soul and spirit, as shall cause you to have no joy at all of the light, no list to look up to heaven. See Chap. 13.10. Amos 8.9,10. both may well stand.

*{moon withdraw itself:*} As to her withdrawing chamber; as of the sun, Psal. 19.6. Heb. *shall not be gathered up*; as chap. 57.1. Or, *shall not retire*, or, *get her away*; as Num. 11.30. *Moses retired*, or, *got himself away into the camp*.

*{for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light,*} As before, ver. 19.

*{and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.*} Chap. 35.10. & 40.2. & 54.9. Rev. 7.16,17. & 21.4.

**V. 21.** *{Thy people also shall be all righteous:*} Heb. *And* (as verse 17.) *thy people all they*, (for, *all shall be*; the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive: as Jer. 4.22. & 9.3. & 35.8. which therefore need not be written in a different character) *righteous*. Such shall all be, that are free denizens of the heavenly Jerusalem. See chap. 4.3. & 62.12. Jer. 31.23. Eph. 2.19. Rev. 21.27.

*{they shall inherit the land for ever:*} The new world, by Christ renewed and restored, in a special manner here, in full perfection hereafter; whereof that of Canaan was a type, Chap. 57.13. & 65.17,18. 2 Pet. 3.13. Rev. 21.5,7. Some would have the words read; *Thy people all the just of them, shall inherit the land for ever*; as Psal. 37.29. but the pauses, in the Hebrew, will not admit it.

*{the branch of my planting, the work of my hands that I may be glorified.*} There is here a twofold reading; the one in the text, the other in the margin. The text has, *his planting*, which some retaining, thus read, and render it; *That the branch of his plant may glory in, or, through the work of my hands*: and of these, some, by *the branch*, here spoken of, understand Christ, chap. 11.1. whom all the faithful being grafted into, Rom. 6.5. & 11.17,24. do, through God's blessing on them, become a most glorious plantation, ch. 61.3. Others, by it understand the issue and posterity of God's people, that should glory in God's doings for them, and benefits conferred on them, Psal. 44.8. But the most, following that in the margin, *my planting*; do, some render the words, as our version has them; some, with little difference, *they are*, or *shall be, a branch of my plantings, a work of my hands; wherein I will glory*. Others, *that the branch of my planting, the work of my hands may be glorified*; and some would have it to be as a reason rendered why they should so continue in possession of that inheritance before mentioned, either taken from the time past: God himself has planted them therein, and therefore would not suffer them to be wholly rooted out of it again, Psal. 44.2. & 80.2. chap. 5.2. because he would plant it, and so plant it, that he might glory of it, and in it; which he could not do, if he should suffer it, to be pluck up, or rooted out, Mat. 15.13. & 16.18. The words are thus precisely in the original; *A branch of my plantations, a work of my hands to glory in*, that is, my people, being (as by apposition joined to what went before) *a branch of my special plantation* (for these plurals usually import an eminency, and excellency, in each kind. See Prov. 1.20.) *my handiwork* (my masterpiece) wherein I intend to *show myself magnificent* or *glorious*, chap. 49.3. the word is the same with that, ver. 7. and chap. 61.3.

**V. 22.** *{A little one shall become a thousand; and a small one a strong nation.*} So reading the words, the sense should be; that the church should grow, not in number only, but in strength and stature too; which is true indeed, Zach. 12.4. Eph. 3.16. & 4.13,15. But the two members of the sentence here seem rather to be, in substance the same; the word rendered *strong*, signifying no other than *numerous*; as Joel 1.6. See on Chap. 16.14. And it implies only a miraculous multiplication of the church, chap. 66.7,8. Jer. 31.27. Act. 2.41. & 4.4. & 5.14. as if a small family consisting but of a few persons, should suddenly, or in short time, become a numerous nation, chap. 66.7,8. Some would have the meaning to be, that men but of weak parts, and small gifts, shall convert many, Act. 11.20,21. But the former seems the native sense.

*{I the Lord will hasten it in his time*} This is added, that they may not doubt of the doing of it, in regard of the improbability: or, as might be deemed, the impossibility of it, chap. 66.8. he will do it, with whom nothing is hard to be done, Num. 11.23. Jer. 32.27. he will speedily effect it, when its due time is come; and till then, they must expect, chap. 13.22. & 8.17. & 28.16. & 30.18. Hab. 2.3. Luk. 1.20.

### CHAPTER 61

**Ver. 1.** *{The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me:*} This chapter, much of the same argument with the former, consists of three parts, 1. Christ's calling to his ministry, and the exercise of his prophetical office, shadowed out in Esay's, ver. 1–3. 2. The restitution, increase, and growth of the church of God, under him, ver. 4–9. And 3. a solemn acknowledgment made in the church's name, of the manifold blessings, by God bestowed on her, ver. 10,11.

*{The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me:*} This is not the Jewish commenters only, but a great part of our interpreters also, conceive to be spoken by Esay of himself. Herein they differ only, that the former restrain it unto Esay; the latter extend it unto Christ, as more perfectly, and consummately, fulfilled in him. And it is true, that other of God's ministers, and messengers, had the Spirit of God in them, and on them, and spoke by it, 2 Sam. 23.2. 2 Chr. 20.14. & 24.10. ch. 63.11. 1 Pet. 1.11. 2 Pet. 1.19. but Christ in a far more abundant, and transcendent manner and measure, constantly resting on him, and residing in him, ch. 11.2. & 42.1. Joh. 1.33. & 3.34. who therefore also in more special manner applies this Scripture unto himself, Luk. 4.18. in regard whereof divers interpreters, on the other side restrain it wholly unto him; of whom, that it is principally intended, I suppose, cannot be denied; though not excluding Esay, who had this Spirit on him, when he spoke it: Nor the apostles, unto whom Christ imparted of the same Spirit, for the work of their Apostleship, both before his ascension, in a competency, Joh. 20.22. and after his ascension in a far more plentiful manner, Act. 2.4,33. as before his passion, and again after his resurrection, he had formerly promised, Joh. 14.16,17,26. & 15.26. & 16.7. Luk. 24.49. Act. 1.5,8. 1 Thess. 4.8.

*{because the Lord hath anointed me.*} Of this spiritual unction, in a competent measure of sanctifying grace, do all the faithful, each one according to his degree and proportion, partake, Psal. 105.15. 2 Cor. 1.21,22. 1 Joh. 2.20,27. But there is, besides this general unction, a more special anointing, by which some are anointed, and endowed with some special gifts and graces, for the discharge of special places and offices; a thing typified in those material unctions, whereby men were, in times past, solemnly set apart unto employments of note and weight, in church and state, Lev. 8.12. Num. 11.17,25. 1 Sam. 10.1,6,9. & 16.13. In either kind, was Christ, as man, anointed, in far more large, eminent, and excellent manner, than any other, Psal. 45.7. Act. 10.38. Col. 2.3,9. Heb. 1.8. and thereby set apart to the work of the Mediatorship, and to be a King, Priest, and Prophet, unto God's people, being furnished with all endowments necessary for the discharge of those offices, and with a superabundant redundancy also, for the conveyance of a sufficiency of such endowments unto others, for the spiritual behoof, both of themselves, and others, Dan. 9.2.4. Joh. 1.16. & 10.26. & 17.19. Thus was he anointed from his very conception, and the assumption of his flesh, by the Word, in the womb of his mother, Luk. 1.35. Joh. 1.14. but it was in a more open and solemn manner, publicly declared and manifested, when at his baptism, being now to enter upon the exercise, and execution of his office, the Holy Ghost, in a visible form, descended, and rested upon him, shortly after which also he preached upon this text, and applied it unto himself, Mat. 3.16,17. Joh. 1.32,33. Luk. 3.22. & 4.1,14,18,21. the same Spirit being afterward sent by him, did in a visible shape light upon his apostles, and rested likewise on them, Act. 2.3,4. who may well also be said, to have been anointed therewith: as also was Esay undoubtedly before his mission unto the prophetical function, who might therefore truly say this of himself, as well as that, chap. 50.4.

*{anointed me to preach*} A complexive form of speech: *anointed*; that is, not fitted, and furnished me only with abilities for such an employment; but set apart, assigned, appointed, and sent me also so to do. See the phrase used of Eliseus, 1 King. 19.16,19,20. (where yet no use of any material oil is found) compared with 2 King. 2.9,15. & so it may be truly averred of Esay, that he was so fitted and furnished, so set apart, and so sent, chap. 6.8,9. & 48.16. to preach, both the corporal deliverance from the Babylonian thraldom; and the spiritual deliverance, from the service of sin and Satan, by Christ, which so frequently he does. But Christ, in a far more ample, excellent, and efficacious manner; not to preach and publish these things only, as Esay, to foretell them, but himself also to effect them, Joh. 3.16,17,34. & 4.34. & 5.23,24,30,36–38. & 6.27,29,38–40. and 7.16,17,28,29. & 8.26,29,42. & 10.36. Gal. 4.4. 1 Pet. 1.20. And for their function and employment, had his apostles also a mission from him, with whom, and others his ministers, their successors, he promised to go along, and to cooperate with them, by his Spirit to the world's end, Mat. 28.18–20. Mar. 15.15,16. Joh. 29.21. in regard whereof, he is also said to come, and preach by them, Eph. 2.17. and to speak in them, 2 Cor. 13.3. that which our prophet also foretold should be, chap. 59.21.

*{to preach good tidings unto the meek*} Of the word here rendered, *to preach good tidings*, see on chap. 40.9. & 52.7. it is a word of middle notion, but used most in the better part: From the Greek word answering to it, so taken, has the gospel (with us also so termed not as *God-spell*, or *God’s-word*; but as *God-spell*, that is, *Good-spell*) its name, preached, by God himself, to Abraham, Gal. 3.8. by Esay, and other the prophets, to the ancient Jewish people, Act. 5.24. Rom. 16.25,26. Heb. 4.2. by the Angels to the shepherds, Luk. 2.10. by our Savior, in person, to the Jews of his time, Luke 4.43. & 8.1. and by his apostles afterward, having from him commission so to do, both to Jews and Gentiles, Act. 13.32. & 15.7. & 20.24. 1 Thess. 2.9. and what is therefore said here of preaching *good tidings* to *the meek*, is by our Savior, said in terms not much discrepant from the same, that *the poor have the good tidings* of the gospel *preached to them*, Mat. 11.5. Luk. 7.22. by *poor* understanding, not the *poor* simply alone, Luk. 6.20. but, the *poor* also *in spirit*, Mat. 5.3. and so what our version here, according to the Hebrew, has *meek*, both the ancient Greek, and the Evangelist also render *poor*, Luk. 4.18. as those two words in Hebrew, coming from the same root, are in letters, and notion, very near the one to the other. Neither are any other intended, by the one term, or the other, but such as were described, chap. 57.15. such as *with meekness receive the word* of salvation, Jam. 1.21. this meekness of spirit being a note of those, to whom God shows mercy, and imparts grace, Psal. 10.17. & 22.26. & 25.9. & 37.11. & 76.9. & 147.6. Prov. 3.34. chap. 11.4. & 29.19. Zeph. 2.3. and are by our Savior therefore pronounced happy, Mat. 5.5. See on chap. 11.4. where both words are found, and used as a parallel.

*{he hath sent me*} This is added, as a further and fuller explication, or expression, of what was before implied, and included in the term of *anointing*: of both Esay's and Christ's mission and commission, see there.

*{to bind up the broken hearted;*} Such as are humbled and brought low by affliction and anguish, and thoroughly touched with a lively sense of their sins, the procuring cause thereof, chap. 50.4. & 57.15. Mat. 11.28. it is a metaphor taken, from the practice of surgery, in the binding up of wounds, to assuage the pain of them, and cause them to close; or the binding up, and swathing of bones, that are broken or disjointed, as to give ease, so to set and knit them again: For that which is said here *to bind*, the old Greek and the Evangelist, Luk. 4.18. have *to heal*; whence some interpreters make it a complexive term and render it, *by binding up to heal*, they are both joined together, Psal. 147.3. where the same form of speech is used. See of *binding up* the like metaphor, chap. 1.6. & 3.7. & 30.26. Job 5.17. Ezek. 30.21. & 34.4. Hos. 6.4. and of inward *brokenness*, in allusion to the like of bones in the body, Psal. 51.8,19. Jer. 23.9.

*{to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound:*} Temporal freedom by Cyrus from the Babylonian captivity, chap. 45.13. & 49.9. spiritual deliverance from the thraldom of sin, and Satan, by Christ, Joh. 8.32,34. Rom. 6.17,18. Col. 1.13. 2 Tim. 2.26.

*{the opening of the prison*} There are here, in the original, two terms knit together, with such a joint, as does generally join divers words together: Whence some of our Jewish critics would have here two several words: and of these, the former to signify *opening*, the latter, to signify, as some, *a prison*; as others, *a prey*, as others, *taking*, or, *taking out*; and so to import, not a bare opening of the place of restraint only, but a letting, or setting, loose also out of it. But the most of them, because the latter word in neither notion is anywhere at all found, would make it all but one word, the letters of the latter part of it, being redoubled, as in divers other words to add some emphasis thereunto: To whom I should agree, did I find in any other word of the like mold, such a division of the syllables one from another, as here, with the like line between. But wanting as yet such an instance, I concur rather with the former, supposing the words to be twain, and the latter to signify, *a prison* (though not elsewhere found, as many other in this prophet) so called of *taking*, or receiving, and, retaining, or keeping persons under restraint. So a learned man, skilled in those languages, informs us, that a word from the same root, with this, is in the Ethiopic tongue, used for *bonds*, Mat. 5.25. Mar. 5.4. and that sometime joined with the word *house*, Act. 5.19. sometime simply without it, for *a prison*, Mat. 14.10. Again, because a word, from the same root, whence this is deemed to come, with a letter servient only, and prefixed, is used, for *prey*, chap. 49.24,25. and the word, *prey*, may comprehend as well men, as beasts, Num. 31.11. where it is used of both; some therefore would here so expound it, *to open the prey*, that is, *to set the captive at liberty*: the same that was before mentioned: as *the captive* is said to be *opened*, or, *loosed*, chap. 51.14. Whereunto may be added, that the word here used, with a very small change, and that not unusual, does in the Chaldee signify, *a leash* or thong, of leather: and with such, captives and slaves were wont to be bound. See chap. 58.6. The former word, that has in it a notion of *opening*, is most frequently used of opening the eyes to see; as chap. 35.5. & 37.16. once only of the ears, chap. 42.20. which the ancient Greek, it seems, taking notice of, renders the words here, *sight*, or, *seeing again*, or, *looking up to the blind*: Whence some imagine, that such as live in dark dungeons as being in the same condition with blind ones, having no more use of light, or sight, the one, than the other, might therefore, by them be so styled: Though others conceive, that some parallel places being noted, by some in the margin: as this from Chap. 42.7. *to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of prison*: and another, from chap. 58.6. did after, in some transcripts, creep into the text: they are both exhibited in the Greek, by the Evangelist, Luk. 4.8.

**V. 2.** *{To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord*} So Luk. 4.19. Heb. *the year of liking*, or, *good will*, or, *acceptance*, as chap. 56.7. *of good will*; as, *a time of liking*, or, *good will*, Psal. 69.13. chap. 49.5. and, *a day of liking*, or, *good will*, or, *acceptance*, Chap. 58.5. the time in which God is pleased to offer and exhibit favor and grace, to render and extend mercy and goodness, to mankind, chap. 60.22. Psal. 102.13. Gal. 4.4. Tit. 3.4. *year*; as, *day*, afterward, in a latitude, for *time*: as chap. 34.8. & 63.4. and these, among the ancients, are much out of the way therefore, who would hence collect, some of them, that Christ preached but one year in all, after his baptism, called here *the Lord's year of acceptance*. Other of them, that he preached two years: the one whereof is here termed, *a year of acceptance*, in opposition unto, or distinction from the other, that was not such: but by *year*, is no such limited list of time here intended, nor is the assertion itself consonant to the truth of story: it being apparent, by the number of Passovers therein upon record, that our Savior preached years, more than one or two. But the word, *year*, here, seems to have some reference to the year of Jubilee, a year of general releasement, proclaimed by sound of trumpet, wherein every man was to return to his inheritance again, and every servant to his freedom, Le. 25.9,10,40,41,54.

*{and the day of vengeance of our God*} The time wherein he will take vengeance for his people, upon their oppressors; the deliverance of the one, and the destruction of the other, going usually together. See chap. 14.1. So chap. 63.4. & 66.14. for they are very wide, who by *vengeance*, would understand here, nothing less, than what the word itself generally imports, nothing that savors of hatred, or harshness: but a kind and equal retribution of ease, and good, to God's people, for the evil, and hardship, which they had formerly sustained, Luk. 16.25. 2 Thess. 1.6,7. and this they ground principally on this, that the Evangelist, Luk. 4.19. has *retribution*; for that which is here rendered *vengeance*: and it is true, that their old Latin so has it there; as the ancient Greek also renders it: but neither is that clause, at all, in the Greek copies, of Luke: nor does the word of *retribution*, necessarily import matter of good, or benefit, being so frequently used of *vengeance*, and evil, Judg. 1.7. Psal. 7.4. chap. 65.6,7. Jer. 25.14. & 51.24. See chap. 34.8. & 59.18.

*{to comfort all that mourn*} All Sion's mourners, chap. 57.18. ver. 3. Mat. 5.4. Luk. 6.14.

**V. 3.** *{To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion*} Or, *for Zion*; either for the evils committed in her, Ezek. 9.4. or, for the evils, thereby procured unto her, chap. 66.10. Heb. *to the mourners of Zion*, or, *to Zion's mourners*; as chap. 57.18. the sentence seems defective, and something needful to be supplied; that the verb rendered, *appoint*, may pass unto: and such defects we meet with sometime, as *take*, for, *take food*, Gen. 42.33. *break*, for *break bread*, Jer. 16.7. In the old Latin copies therefore was inserted *strength*; *to put strength to them that mourn in Zion*. But because *strength* seems not to suit so well with *mourning*, or, *mourners*: for that is not the matter, that, as mourners, they need, some other rather, from the former verse, supply *consolation*; rendering the text, *to exhibit consolation to Zion's mourners*: and this seems most genuine. Though there want not those, that would carry on this, to that which follows, as having reference to all the ensuing particulars; *to appoint unto those that mourn in Zion, to give*, I say, *unto them*: that is, to such, &c.

*{to give unto them beauty for ashes*} To assign them *ornaments* or *bravery*, (so the word properly signifies, chap. 3.18,20. Ezek. 24.17,23.) such fair and goodly apparel, as they used to wear on better days, or when no special occasion of grief, or mourning, Exod. 33.5. *for ashes*; or instead of ashes: a sign of sadness and mourning, chap. 58.5. Lam. 2.10. Job 2.12. & 42.6. Mat. 11.21. there is a sweet elegancy in the original, between the two terms here used, which our English cannot express. The meaning is, to alter their condition from sadness to gladness; from mourning to mirth: and accordingly to alter their habit, and weed, whereby either is usually expressed, Psal. 30.11.

*{the oil of joy for mourning*} *The oil of joy*, or *gladness*, Psal. 45.2. such ointment as they used to anoint their heads, and faces with, to make them look more cheerfully, and with the fragrancy thereof, to refresh their spirits, in their festivals, or when they desired to show themselves frolic and cheerful, Psal. 104.15. 2 Sam. 12.20. Eccl. 7.1. & 9.8. Mat. 6.17.

*{the garments of praise*} White and fair garments, Eccl. 9.8. fit for festivals, and triumph, Zach. 3.4,5. Mat. 22.11. Luk. 15.22. Rev. 3.4. an outward sign of a *merry heart*, of a lightsome, and cheerful spirit within, Ecc. 9.7.

*{for the spirit of heaviness:*} Heb. *of dimness*, Gen. 27.1. Deut. 34.7. chap. 42.3. Zach. 11.17. or, *of contraction*, Lev. 13.6,21,26,39,56. because grief contracts and draws in, as joy widens and dilates, chap. 65. So Ezek. 21.7. *every spirit shall contract itself*.

*{that they may be called*} Heb. *and* (as ver. 4.) *it shall be called to them*, or, *of them*; that is, *that they may be*; as chap. 60.18. ver. 6. so known, so accounted, and so acknowledged, ver. 9.

*{trees of righteousness*} Or, *oaks*, as some. See chap. 1.29,30. & 6.13. *trees of righteousness*; that is, trees of just, full, fair, firm, strength, and stature. See chap. 57.5. as, *sacrifices of righteousness*, Deut. 33.19. Psal. 4.5. & 51.19. that is, just, entire, complete ones, Psal. 69.31. or, *firmly rooted, in righteousness*, as some, Eph. 7.17. not like the grain, on the stony ground, without root, Mat. 13.6,21. or, as others, filled with, and abounding in, *fruits of righteousness*, Phil. 1.11. such as bring forth fruit, whereby God may be glorified, Mat. 3.8. & 7.17. & 12.23. Joh. 15.5,8. all which, the spiritual sense may include; but the literal I conceive to be, what was first propounded; to wit, in the first place, the flourishing and prosperous estate of God's people, discovering even to the natural eye, God's blessing upon them.

*{the planting of the Lord*} Or, *the Lord's plantation*: not fair only, but firm, such as may, by the thriving, flourishing, and lasting, of it, show whose handiwork it is, Num. 24.6. Psal. 92.13,14. & 104.16. See chap. 60.21. ver. 9.

*{that he might be glorified.*} As he is by the good works, and well-doings of his people, Mat. 5.16. Joh. 15.8. Phil. 1.11. Yet the words rather are, *that he may glory in them*, or, *show himself goodly, and magnificent in them*, by causing them to thrive, and prosper, and flourish, as Ps. 1.3. Jer. 17.8. See ch. 44.23. where the same word is used.

**V. 4.** *{And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations; and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations.*} Or, *that they may build, and raise up, and repair*: as, *That they may be called*, ver. 3. That being set at liberty, returning again to their own country, they may re-edify the cities, and towns, that have been ruinated, and both people, and plant again their land, and grounds, that have lain long waste, and desolate. So Chap. 44.26. & 49.17,19. & 51.3. & 52.9. and 58.12.

*{the old wastes*} Heb. *wastes of perpetuity*: of long continuance, Jer. 49.13. above a Jubilee time consisting but of fifty years, at most, Lev. 25.9,10. expressed by the term here used, Exod. 21.6.

*{the waste cities*} Heb. *cities of wasteness*: as Lev. 26.31,32. *your cities shall be wasteness*; that is, *cities of wasteness*; utterly wasted.

*{desolations of many generations*} Heb. *of generation and generation*; as chap. 60.15. those places that had lain a long time desolate. See chap. 58.12.

**V. 12.** *{And strangers shall stand, and feed your flocks; and the sons of the alien, shall be your plowmen, and your vinedressers.*} That is, as some; You shall have generally so fair, and plentiful estates, that you shall not need to make use of other than strangers, either hired, or bought, or taken in war, for any servile, or meaner sort of employments. See chap. 14.2. Zach. 2.8,9. which some also applying to the state, and condition of the church, under Christ, thus expound it, That, those that in former times, have used Christian people hardly, and harshly, depriving them of their means, and livelihood, making slaves of them, should then, submitting themselves to them, willingly and sedulously apply themselves, to do them any pleasure, to be any way serviceable unto them; as the Gibeonites were sometime unto the Israelites, Josh. 9.23,27. from whose example, some restrain it to such strangers, as living in the church, though not incorporate into it, yet should be serviceable thereunto. See chap. 60.10. Others extending it yet farther, and taking it in a larger notion, conceive the meaning to be; that having applied themselves to look after the things concerning the Kingdom of God, and what especially appertained thereunto; other necessaries concerning this present life, should some way or other, be as certainly, and sufficiently provided for them, as if they had such to do all this for them, Mat. 6.33. but we need not strain the words so far. What some others have of the spiritual husbandry, wherein strangers are now most employed, 1 Cor. 3.6–9. or, of a new ministry settled in room of the former, now abolished, Mat. 21.41. seem to run counter to the text: *strangers*; and *sons of an alien*, seem here the same; as Chapter 3.6. and 56.3,6.

*{stand*} As servants waiting and attending on their master, ready to go, and run, at his beck, or to be enjoined what service he pleases. See chap. 6.2. or, *stand, and feed*; that is, *stand feeding*: attend the feeding of your cattle; as, *they faint, they lie*, for, *they lie fainting*, chap. 51.20. and, *stand, and snuff up the wind*, for, *stand snuffing up the wind*, Jer. 14.6.

**V. 6.** *{But ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord; men shall call you the ministers of our God*} Heb. *And ye*, (as chap. 60.10.) or, *As for you*, (as chap. 57.3.) *Priests of Jehovah shall ye be called; Ministers of our God are ye, shall it be said unto you*; or, *Ministers of God shall it be said of you*: as Num. 23.23. ch. 19.18. & 62.4. Joh. 13.13. where the syntax seems the same with this: *to be called* such, for so to be, and so accounted, as before, v. 3. Now this some restrain unto the priests and Levites, of whom, chap. 52.11. as if it were said, You that are God's priests and ministers, though you be now in contempt and disgrace, shall then be in repute, and be plentifully provided for, as in times past, when the Jewish state did most flourish. But these seem to narrow the text too much. Others therefore giving it a larger extent, conceive the meaning to be, that all God's people now should be in that repute abroad, as if they were all priests: as he sometime said of the Roman Senate, that they seemed to be as so many kings; in which sense, or the like to it, some would have the word rendered *Priests*, to be here taken, not for *Priests*, but for *Princes*, or, *chief Rulers*: as some also conceive it to be, Gen. 41.45,50. 2 Sam. 20.26. 1 King. 5.4. and, as it is apparently, where it is used of David's sons, 2 Sam. 8.18. in like manner whereunto, would they have that also to be rendered, Exod. 19.6. *a Kingdom*, not of *Priests*, but of *Princes*; as importing not a sacred, but a noble Kingdom. For whereas they require here, as they suppose also there requisite, a supply of the note of similitude, oft omitted: though it may do, not amiss there, yet neither is it needful, nor suitable here. Others understand it, as an enlargement of honor, and nearer approach unto God, than they had formerly enjoyed: that whereas, before, they were, the main body of them, God's *peculiar people*, Exod. 19.5. Deut. 7.6. & 26.18. and some only of them, set apart for sacred functions, Deut. 10.8. they should now be taken all to be as near to God, and in as honorable a condition, as the priests and Levites, beforetime were; as your whole land, or state, shall be called, *the Lord's Sion*, chap. 60.14. so shall yourselves also be called, and accounted his *Priests*, and Ministers: and if it be said, that they were so said to be, at God's first taking of them, to wit, *a Kingdom of Priests*; (for so the received version aright renders it, confirmed by the apostle, expounding it, *a royal Priesthood*, 1 Pet. 2.9.) the answer may be, that they are there so termed; because the Priesthood was then dispersed, as it were, throughout all their tribes and families; and so the whole body of the nation seemed to share in it; some resemblance whereof seemed to remain in the paschal solemnity, whereat, each head of a family seemed to be as a priest, Exod. 12.3,6. whereas afterward it was confined, for the ministerial employment, in general, unto one tribe, Levi, and for the principal functions thereof, unto one family, Num. 18.6,7,22. that which is in the New Testament, under the Messiah, said, accordingly, to be extended unto all the faithful, as called to be spiritual kings and priests, 1 Pet. 2.9. Heb. 13.15. Rev. 1.6. & 5.10. & 20.6.

*{ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles*} You shall have supplies of all necessaries from them, either subdued by you, as some; or adjoined to you, as others: or from both, as a third sort. See cha. 60.6,7. and this, also some think, has some respect to the priests' manner of maintenance, provided for plentifully, according to God's appointment, by the labor and husbandry of the people, Nu. 18.11–15,21.

*{and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves*} Or, *by their glory shall ye lift up yourselves*, or, *grow lofty*: as those that derive it from a word, deemed to signify, *an uppermost branch*, chap. 17.6,9. it is nowhere found, save here, and Psal. 94.4. You shall be highly advanced, and become very conspicuous, through that honor, that from them, shall accrue unto you, as such uppermost branches, on flourishing trees usually are. See chap. 49.18. & 63.9,11.

**V. 7.** *{For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion, they shall rejoice in their portion; therefore in their land, they shall possess the double:*} Some rent off the former branch of this verse, and annex it to the verse foregoing, thus reading the text; *Ye shall feed on the wealth of the Heathen, and be lift up with their glory; instead of*, or, *in way of recompense, for your shame and confusion*; which among them, and at their hands, you had formerly sustained. What follows, they refer unto the Gentiles coming in to them: *they shall commend their portion*; (that is, rest well apaid, deem themselves fully satisfied, in that, what they have conferred to God's service, is accepted) *because that* (which they shall be, as being assured of this, that) *they shall inherit double in their own land*, (here on earth) *and everlasting joy*; hereafter, Mar. 10.29. Others, so join it to the former, as that they apply it entirely to God's people; they shall have such honor, as was said: and it shall be unto you, or betide you, *in lieu of your double shame, and of that ignominy*, whereof, they (to wit, those heathen, your enemies) did sometime *sing*, saying, *This is your portion*; or that this was their portion; to wit, of God's people, Psal. 44.13–16. These, and divers other readings, for harshness, not unlike them, I forbear to insist on, and hold to the reading that our version exhibits, because it seems, with least force, to flow of itself from the text: all the difficulty is, in the change of the person, which in this prophet is not unusual. See chap. 1.29. & 22.19. & 33.4. & 62.1,2. and here also, ver. 4,5,7. And this admitted, the meaning is plain, the words being thus rendered, *Instead of your shame, double shall be unto you; and, instead of reproach, they shall rejoice of, or, in, their portion: because in their land they shall possess double, and joy everlasting shall be unto them.*

*{for your shame, double*} Some join *shame*, and *double*, together: expounding *double*; some *twofold*: the shame of their land, and the shame of themselves, a reproach lying upon both, Ezek. 36.3,4,13,15. or reproach from the Heathen, and reproach from their own countrymen, unto both whom the profession of Christianity was reproachful, 1 Cor. 1.13. or, misery in themselves, and contempt from others, Psal. 123.3,4. Others, *plentiful, abundant*, and the term is oft so used, chap. 40.2. Jer. 16.18. and 17.18. And so I conceive it here to be taken: but with reference unto that, which in lieu of it they should now receive *double*, to wit, honor, v. 6. that is, large and eminent, as *double honor*, 1 Tim. 5.17. or *a double portion*: supplying it from the next branch; as some of the Jewish doctors supply *possess* from the last; thus rendering the text, *in lieu of your shame, ye shall possess double*: and withal adding, that the ensuing words, are an explication of the same: so God promises to restore *double* to his people, for all their damages that they had formerly sustained, Zach. 9.12. as he did sometime to Job, Job 42.10,12.

*{and for confusion*} Or, *and, in lieu of* (the preposition repeated from the former member, as the verb in the like manner, ch. 60.17.) *their reproach*; because the person is changed; as Job 18.4. Jer. 27.1,2. Ezek. 31.10. the preposition omitted; as chap. 59.18.

*{they shall rejoice in their portion:*} Or, *they shall triumph*: for the word implies a *singing*, or, *sounding*, in triumphant manner, Psal. 33.1. & 118.15. ch. 12.6. & 24.14. See ver. 3. Psal. 126.2. *in their portion*: a defect of the particle; as chap. 34.2. 57.8. in their portion, or inheritance, that they shall then return to, or possess again, as in the Jubilee year, Lev. 25.9,10. alluded to before, ver. 2. as that which for their portion was assigned to them at first, Josh. 19.9. Psal. 16.6. Ezek. 47.13–23. Mich. 2.4.

*{therefore in their land, they shall possess the double:*} This (not to repeat again what of this branch was before said) some make an inference upon the former, in regard of the illative particle, *therefore*; as implying, that because they had undergone *double shame*, therefore they should now receive *double*, whether honor, or what else. But I conceive that the retribution of *double honor*, was before mentioned; and that in this clause is a reason rendered; of their rejoicing in the portion, that they should then receive. And I suppose that the word here rendered, *therefore*, as an illative, should rather be rendered, *because*, as a causal, as of necessity it must be taken, chap. 26.14. Though I find not any, either of the Jewish critics, or ours, that have observed it; *in their land* returning again to it, after their long exilement and absence, *they shall possess double*; they shall possess and enjoy a double portion, either in regard of that blessing of God, upon that which they shall possess, affording double in worth; to what beforetime it did. See chap. 4.2. or, in regard of the large extent of each one's portion to that in former times they held, a great part of them being wasted and worn out, either slain and famished in fight and siege, before the deportation; or consumed in the captivity, and a remnant, some tenth of them only, returning, chap. 6.13. & 10.21,22. & 11.11. and there seems to be in it, an allusion to the Law, concerning the firstborn, that was to have a *double portion*, Deut. 21.17. and to the house of Joseph, that had a *double portion* of inheritance, in the promised land; 1 Chron. 5.1. Josh. 17.17. Ezek. 47.13. as if he had said, it shall be then with each tribe, as it was with the house of Joseph before: and with each of you it shall be, as if he were a *firstborn*; as all the faithful in the gospel are said to be, Heb. 12.23. Howbeit, some understand it, not of their own, but of the Heathen, their enemies' land, not that they should repossess their own land, (though that also they did) but that *in their* (that is, the Heathens') *land, they should possess double*, in way of reparation, for the double damages done them. But I adhere rather to the former.

*{everlasting joy shall be unto them.*} Heb. *joy of perpetuity*. See chap. 35.10.

**V. 8.** *{For I the Lord love judgment,*} There is no great difficulty in the words, or matter of this verse, save in the connection of them, with the rest of the context. Some conceive them to render a reason of what went before; either concerning those strangers, that had contributed to his people, that he would largely, and liberally reward them for it: because they had offered freely, not by constraint, nor of rapine, but of their own lawfully gotten, 2 Cor. 8.3–5. & 9.5,7. Or, concerning his own people, that had amidst their long tedious, and grievous afflictions, continued firm to him, and sincere in his service, whom therefore in equity he could not but affect and requite, 2 Thess. 1.6,7. Heb. 1.10. albeit the unsound ones among them, he deservedly abhorred, chap. 1.11–15. Others, suppose it to contain matter distinct from the former, concerning a further benefit, that God would vouchsafe to confer upon them; to wit the renewing of his Covenant with them, and premising a reason, why, in such manner, he should renew it. So he before closed up his promises of favors to be conferred upon, and in their deliverance, and after their return, Chap. 59.21. Only one learned writer suggests a divers reading, which admitted, will afford a very fit connection of this passage with the former discourse. He thus renders the words, *For I the Lord love right; I hate rapine by iniquity*. So precisely the Greek renders it; and so is the word used in the plural form, Psal. 58.3. & 64.6. and in the singular also lengthened, Job 5.16. Thus the coherence will be smooth; a reason being rendered, why God will right, and repay the wrongs and damages done to his people; because he loves right, and hates such unjust and injurious courses, as had been offered unto them, Psalm 11.5.

*{For*} Or, *Because*; as rendering a reason of what ensues.

*{I the Lord love judgment,*} I love just, upright, and equal, dealing, delight in it, and in those only that practice it, chap. 56.1,2,4. Jer. 9.24. Zach. 8.16,17,19.

*{I hate robbery for burnt-offering:*} I abhor any oblation whatsoever, (one kind put for all, as chap. 56.7.) brought of goods gotten by oppression and wrong, and cannot therefore accept of any service, or sacrifice, tendered to me, by such as practice the same; that which, in former times, arguing their hypocrisy, had made all their solemn rites, and religious performances, so not unacceptably only, but even abominable in God's sight, chap. 1.11–15. & 66.3. Amos 5.21,24. Or, *I hate rapine by iniquity*; the spoiling of persons and people, by injurious courses, as was before specified. See 2 Sam. 3.34–36. Hab. 1.13.

*{and I will direct their work in truth,*} This most, both Jewish, and other interpreters, expound, of God's rendering, or returning a reward to his people, for the misery, and ignominy, that for his sake, they had sustained; as ver. 7. Some other, of God's disposing their affairs, in a successful course, in a prosperous way; and that such as should be constant and permanent, chapter 26.3,12. And that former intimation of God's *hating rapine*, as was last before hinted, will very well sort with either of these. Howbeit, some understand it of God's concurrence with his good Spirit, graciously working upon the hearts of his people, and thereby so disposing, and managing their ways and works, that being performed in sincerity, they might have acceptance, chap. 56.7. the very sum and substance of the new Covenant, or the renewed, and renewing Covenant, hereafter mentioned. See the like, Deut. 30.6. chap. 57.18. Jer. 24.7. & 31.33. & 32.40. Ezek. 36.26,27. Mal. 3.3,4. But I go rather with the former.

*{and*} Or, *therefore*; as chap. 42.25. & 43.12. and so most here render it.

*{I will direct*} Heb. *I will give*; but the Hebrew term is of a very large extent, used commonly, *to make, to appoint, to put, to place, to frame, to direct, to dispose*. See Deut. 28.13. Judg. 15.1. chap. 3.4. & 22.21. & 41.19. & 43.16. & 46.13. and it may well be here rendered, *direct*, or, *dispose*. See Eph. 2.10,23,24.

*{their work*} So the word properly signifies; as Prov. 10.16. & 11.18. Jer. 31.16. nor need we to depart from the proper notion of it, in this place. Howbeit, it is not unfrequently used also for *hire*, or *reward*, of work; as Lev. 19.13. Jer. 22.13. Psalm 109.20. Chap. 40.10. and 49.4. and 62.11. and so many here take it.

*{in truth*} This some refer to God, he will, *in truth*, that is truly, and surely, make their reward good to them; as Judg. 9.15,16. Psal. 69.13. Others, to the reward; he will make their reward to be *in truth*; that is, firm and sure, as chap. 16.5. Others, to their work; he will so frame, direct, and dispose, their work, that it shall be *done in truth*; that is, sincerely, or shall be *in truth*; that is, sound and sincere; as 1 Sam. 12.24. 1 King. 2.4. & 3.6. Psal. 145.18. chap. 10.20. & 38.3. Joh. 4.24. contrary to that which in former times, it had been, chap. 48.1. Others, to their employments, which God would settle in a constant course, and so dispose, that they should be as well, sure as successful. See chap. 39.8.

*{and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.*} Heb. *I will cut out a covenant of perpetuity, or, eternity, to them*. See chap. 55.3. So Jer. 32.40. & 50.5.

**V. 9.** *{And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people. All that see them, shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.*} See chap. 60.21. ver. 3. They shall so grow and multiply, so thrive and prosper, that they shall become very conspicuous, Mat. 5.14,16. and that it shall evidently appear to all that see them, that there goes a blessing of God along with them, Act. 5.13.

*{their seed, and their offspring*} See chap. 44.3.

*{shall be known*} Shall be eminent, conspicuous or famous: the word is used of such, as are of special note, and of whom more special note is taken, than of others, in the places of their resiance, so Psal. 76.1. *God is known in Judah, his name is great in Israel*; and, *her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the Elders of the land*, Prov. 31.23.

*{among the people,*} Heb. *in the midst of the peoples; in the midst*, for, *among*; as cha. 24.13. Jer. 39.14. & 40.6. *peoples*; as chap. 11.10. & 14.2. among peoples of divers and several countries, with whom they shall be mixed, they shall be so eminent, that they shall be known and distinguished from them.

*{the seed which the Lord hath blessed*} Or, *a seed*; (for there is no article here in the text) that (the relative is wanting; as chap. 60.8.) *the Lord blesseth*; that have God's blessing accompanying them. See chap. 44.3. & 65.16,23.

**V. 10.** *{I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God:*} These two last verses, some rent off from this chapter, and prefix to the next; but I see no necessity so to do, since that the subject matter of them suits well with the former discourse. This verse contains a thankful acknowledgment, conceived in the person of the church, of the special favor, and gracious goodness of God, afforded unto her, in such manner, as had been before related, ver. 3–7.

*{greatly rejoice*} Heb. *rejoicing rejoice*; as chap. 66.10. that is, exceedingly rejoice: the affection of God's people, upon their restitution, above described. So ver. 7.

*{in the Lord*} Or, *for him*; because of him; as Psal. 150.2. chap. 47.9. & 57.17.

*{my soul*} For, *myself*; as Psal. 3.2. But the form makes it more emphatical. So Psal. 34.2. Luk. 1.46,47. the same thing to that purpose also repeated, Hab. 3.18.

*{for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation; he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness:*} Or, *with garments of salvation; with a robe of righteousness*: that is, with salvation, as with goodly garments: with righteousness, as with a robe, he has, by his gracious deliverance wrought for me, and his beneficence, plentifully conferred upon me, made me as glorious, and as conspicuous, in the eyes of all that behold me, as if I were arrayed, in the richest and most gorgeous apparel, that is worn by any, at times of greatest solemnity. So Job 29.14. Psal. 132.9,16. & 149.4. Zach. 3.4,5. See chap. 51.9. & 59.17.

*{the robe*} Of this garment, see chap. 59.17.

*{of righteousness,*} That is as some, Christ, who is *our righteousness*; Jer. 23.6. & 33.16. 1 Cor. 1.30. and, *the sun of righteousness*, Mal. 4.2. and whom we are said to *put on*, Rom. 13.14. Gal. 3.27. Rev. 12.1. or, his righteousness to us, and made ours, Phil. 3.9. or, inherent righteousness, exercised, and discovering itself in the lives of God's people, Psal. 132.9. Eph. 6.14. Rev. 19.8.
